title.zh: 卷四十四 蜀書十四 蔣琬費禕姜維傳
title.en: Volume 44: Book of Shu 14 - Biographies of Jiang Wan, Fei Yi, and Jiang Wei
title.raw: 卷四十四 蜀書十四 蔣琬費禕姜維傳 Volume 44: Book of Shu 14 - Biographies of Jiang Wan, Fei Yi, and Jiang Wei

sentences.zh: 蔣琬字公琰，零陵湘鄉人也。

translations.literal: Jiang Wan, courtesy name Gongyan, was a native of Xiangxiang in Lingling.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Wan, courtesy name Gongyan, came from Xiangxiang in Lingling Commandery.

sentences.zh: 弱冠與外弟泉陵劉敏懼知名。

translations.literal: At his capping he and his maternal cousin Liu Min of Quanling together gained renown (the text writes 懼; parallel editions read 俱 ‘together’).
translations.idiomatic: While still young he won local fame alongside his cousin Liu Min of Quanling.

sentences.zh: 琬以州書佐隨先主入蜀，除廣都長。

translations.literal: Wan served as a provincial clerk and followed the Vanguard Lord into Shu; he was appointed magistrate of Guangdu.
translations.idiomatic: He entered Shu as a provincial clerk under Liu Bei and was named magistrate of Guangdu.

sentences.zh: 先主嘗因遊觀奄至廣都，見琬眾事不理，時又沉醉，先主大怒，將加罪戮。

translations.literal: The Vanguard Lord once on a pleasure outing suddenly arrived at Guangdu and saw Wan leaving official business unattended and at the time also deeply drunk; the Vanguard Lord was greatly angry and was about to impose punishment and execution.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Bei came to Guangdu on a tour, found Jiang Wan drunk and neglecting his duties, and was ready to execute him.

sentences.zh: 軍師將軍諸葛亮請曰：「蔣琬，社稷之器，非百里之才也。

translations.literal: Army commander Zhuge Liang pleaded, saying, "Jiang Wan is vessel of the altars of soil and grain—not talent for a hundred li.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuge Liang intervened: "Jiang Wan is material for the empire, not a petty county magistrate."

sentences.zh: 其為政以安民為本，不以修飾為先，願主公重加察之。

translations.literal: His governing takes pacifying the people as root, not ornament as first; wish the lord examine him again carefully.
translations.idiomatic: He rules by putting the people at ease, not by polished appearances—please look again, my lord."

sentences.zh: 」先主雅敬亮，乃不加罪，倉卒但免官而已。

translations.literal: " The Vanguard Lord always respected Liang and therefore did not add punishment; in haste he only dismissed from office.
translations.idiomatic: " Liu Bei yielded to Zhuge Liang and spared him—stripping him of office alone."

sentences.zh: 琬見推之後，夜夢有—牛頭在門前，流血滂沱，意甚惡之，呼問占夢趙直。

translations.literal: After Wan was promoted, he dreamed at night of an ox head before the gate, bleeding profusely—his intent felt very ill; he called to ask dream-diviner Zhao Zhi.
translations.idiomatic: After his promotion Jiang Wan dreamed of a bloody ox head at his gate and consulted Zhao Zhi about it.

sentences.zh: 直曰：「夫見血者，事分明也。

translations.literal: Zhi said, "Seeing blood means affairs are clear-cut.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Zhi said blood in a dream means matters stand revealed."

sentences.zh: 牛角及鼻，『公』字之象，君位必當至公，大吉之征也。

translations.literal: Ox horn and nose are images of the character ‘public’; your position must reach utmost fairness—a greatly auspicious sign.
translations.idiomatic: Horns and snout sketch the word ‘duke’—you are destined for high, impartial office; most auspicious."

sentences.zh: 」頃之，為什邡令。

translations.literal: " Shortly thereafter he became magistrate of Shifang.
translations.idiomatic: " Soon he was appointed magistrate of Shifang."

sentences.zh: 先主為漢中王，琬人為尚書郎。

translations.literal: When the Vanguard Lord became King of Hanzhong, Wan entered as gentleman of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Bei took the title King of Hanzhong, Jiang Wan became a secretary in the imperial secretariat.

sentences.zh: 建興元年，丞相亮開府，辟琬為東曹掾。

translations.literal: Jianxing first year, Chancellor Liang opened office, summoned Wan as eastern bureau clerk.
translations.idiomatic: In Jianxing 1 (223 CE) Chancellor Zhuge Liang opened his headquarters and appointed Jiang Wan clerk of the eastern bureau.

sentences.zh: 舉茂才，琬固讓劉邕、陰化、龐延、廖淳，亮教答曰：「思惟背親捨德，以殄百姓，眾人既不隱於心，實又使遠近不解其義，是以君宜顯其功舉，以明此選之清重也。

translations.literal: Recommended abundant talent—Wan firmly yielded to Liu Yong, Yin Hua, Pang Yan, Liao Chun; Liang instructed reply saying: "Thinking consider betray kin abandon virtue, thereby destroy hundred surnames—crowd already not hidden in heart; truly also cause far near not understand its meaning—therefore lord should display this merit recommendation, thereby clarify this selection's purity weight."
translations.idiomatic: Nominated as "abundant talent," Jiang Wan insisted the honor go to Liu Yong, Yin Hua, Pang Yan, or Liao Chun. Zhuge Liang answered: "If worthy men hid their light and turned their backs on the people, neither the court nor the countryside would understand—accept the nomination and show how seriously this selection is taken."

sentences.zh: 」遷為參軍。

translations.literal: " Then transferred as army adviser.
translations.idiomatic: " He was promoted to army adviser.

sentences.zh: 五年，亮住漢中，琬與長史張裔統留府事。

translations.literal: Fifth year, Liang dwelt Hanzhong; Wan together with chief clerk Zhang Yi governed remaining office affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year (227 CE) Zhuge Liang moved to Hanzhong; Jiang Wan and chief clerk Zhang Yi ran the rear headquarters.

sentences.zh: 八年，代裔為長史，加撫軍將軍。

translations.literal: Eighth year, replaced Yi as chief clerk; added general who stabilizes the army.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he succeeded Zhang Yi as chief clerk and received the title general who stabilizes the army.

sentences.zh: 亮數外出，琬常足食足兵以相供給。

translations.literal: Liang repeatedly went out abroad; Wan constantly full food full weapons thereby mutually supplied.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Zhuge Liang marched out, Jiang Wan kept grain and weapons flowing without fail.

sentences.zh: 亮每言：「公琰托志忠雅，當與吾共贊王業者也。

translations.literal: Liang each time said: "Gongyan entrusts ambition loyal refined—ought with me together assist kingly enterprise."
translations.idiomatic: Zhuge Liang often said, "Gongyan is loyal and cultivated—he is the man to help me sustain the kingly enterprise."

sentences.zh: 」密表後主曰：「臣若不幸，後事宜以付琬。」

translations.literal: " Secret memorial Later Lord saying: "Your servant if unlucky—after affairs should entrust to Wan."
translations.idiomatic: " He secretly memorialized the emperor: "If I die, let Jiang Wan carry what follows."

sentences.zh: 亮卒，以琬為尚書令，俄而加行都護、假節、領益州刺史、遷大將軍、錄尚書事、封安陽亭侯。

translations.literal: Liang died; appointed Wan as director of the masters; shortly added acting protector-general, credential staff, concurrent Yi province inspector; promoted grand general, records masters affairs, enfeoffed village marquis of Anyang.
translations.idiomatic: After Zhuge Liang's death Jiang Wan became director of the masters, soon acting protector-general with credential staff and concurrent inspector of Yi—then grand general with authority over the masters and village marquis of Anyang.

sentences.zh: 時新喪元帥，遠近危悚。

translations.literal: At time newly lost commander-in-chief; far near peril afraid.
translations.idiomatic: The empire had just lost its commander; fear ran from the capital to the frontier.

sentences.zh: 琬出類拔萃，處群僚之右，既無戚容，又無喜色，神守舉止，有如平日，由是眾望漸服。

translations.literal: Wan stood out from class gathered—placed among crowd officials' right; neither sorrow appearance nor joy color; spirit guard bearing deportment—like ordinary days—thereby crowd hope gradually submitted.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Wan towered above his peers yet showed neither grief nor elation—bearing exactly as before—until expectation across the court turned to trust.

sentences.zh: 延熙元年，詔琬曰：「寇難未弭，曹睿驕凶，遼東三郡勞其暴虐，遂相糾結，與之離隔。

translations.literal: Yanxi first year, edict to Wan saying: "Bandit hardship not ended; Cao Rui arrogant fierce—Liaodong three commanderies labor under his cruelty—thereupon mutually joined together—with him separated."
translations.idiomatic: In Yanxi 1 (238 CE) an edict told Jiang Wan: "The foe remains; Cao Rui is arrogant and cruel—the three Liaodong commanderies suffer his tyranny and have broken away from Wei."

sentences.zh: 睿大興眾役，還相攻伐。

translations.literal: Rui greatly raised crowd labor—returned mutually attack strike.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Rui has drafted vast labor levies and turned armies against his own people.

sentences.zh: 囊秦之亡，勝、廣首難，今有此變，斯乃天時。

translations.literal: Former Qin's perishing—Sheng and Guang first hardship—now having this change—this then Heaven's season.
translations.idiomatic: When Qin fell, Chen Sheng and Wu Guang struck first—today's revolt is Heaven's opening.

sentences.zh: 君其治嚴，總帥諸軍屯任漢中，須吳舉動，東西掎角，以乘其畔。

translations.literal: Lord please govern strict; overall command various armies garrison duty Hanzhong—wait Wu's movements—east west drag horn—thereby ride their rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Train your troops hard, command the armies from Hanzhong, watch Wu's moves, and pinch Wei east and west when opportunity ripens.

sentences.zh: 」又命琬開府，明年就加為大司馬。

translations.literal: " Also ordered Wan open office; next year then added as grand marshal.
translations.idiomatic: " He authorized Jiang Wan to open his own headquarters; the next year he added the title grand marshal.

sentences.zh: 東曹掾楊戲索性簡略，琬與言論，時不應答。

translations.literal: Eastern Bureau aide Yang Xi was by nature terse; when Wan conversed with him he sometimes did not answer.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Xi of the Eastern Bureau was blunt and sparing of words; he often failed to reply when Jiang Wan spoke to him.

sentences.zh: 或欲構戲於琬，曰：「公與戲語而不見應，戲之慢上，不亦甚乎!」琬曰：「人心不同，各如其面；

translations.literal: Some wished to frame Xi before Wan, saying, "You speak with Xi and he does not respond—is not Xi’s disrespect to superiors extreme!" Wan said, "Men’s hearts differ, each like its face;
translations.idiomatic: Some tried to poison Jiang Wan against Yang Xi: "He ignores you—is that not gross insolence?" Jiang Wan replied: "Every mind is different, like every face;"

sentences.zh: 面從後言，古人之所誡也。

translations.literal: face-concurring then later speaking—this is what ancients warned against.
translations.idiomatic: to agree to one’s face and gossip behind one’s back is what the classics condemn."

sentences.zh: 戲欲贊吾是耶，則非其本心，欲反吾言，則顯吾之非，是以默然，是戲之快也。

translations.literal: If Xi wished to praise my being right, then it would not be his true heart; if he wished to oppose my words, then it would display my wrong—therefore silent; this is Xi’s forthrightness.
translations.idiomatic: If he praised me he would flatter against his conscience; if he contradicted me he would expose my faults—so he stayed silent. That is Yang Xi’s honesty."

sentences.zh: 」又督農楊敏曾毀琬，曰：「作事憒憒；

translations.literal: " Also agricultural overseer Yang Min once slandered Wan, saying, "His conduct is muddled;
translations.idiomatic: " The agriculture intendant Yang Min had called Jiang Wan muddled in office;"

sentences.zh: 誠非及前人。

translations.literal: truly he does not reach the former men.
translations.idiomatic: swearing he fell short of his predecessors."

sentences.zh: 」或以白琬，主者請推治敏。

translations.literal: " Someone reported this to Wan; the presiding official requested to pursue and punish Min.
translations.idiomatic: When word reached Jiang Wan, his clerks wanted Yang Min prosecuted."

sentences.zh: 琬曰：「吾實不如前人，無可推也。

translations.literal: Wan said, "I truly do not reach the former men—nothing to pursue.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Wan said: "He is right—I am no match for Zhuge Liang; there is nothing to investigate."

sentences.zh: 」主者重據聽不推，則乞問其憒憒之狀。

translations.literal: " The presiding official pressed again that if not pursuing, then beg to ask the appearance of the muddledness.
translations.idiomatic: They pressed again: if there would be no trial, at least ask what ‘muddled’ meant."

sentences.zh: 琬曰：「苟其不如，則事不當理，事不當理，則憒憒矣。

translations.literal: Wan said, "If he is not as good, then affairs are not rightly ordered; if affairs are not rightly ordered, then it is muddled.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Wan answered: "If I fall short, my government must be confused—that is all ‘muddled’ means."

sentences.zh: 復何問邪?」後敏坐事系獄，眾人猶懼其必死。

translations.literal: What need ask again?" Later Min sat for an affair and was imprisoned; the crowd still feared he would surely die.
translations.idiomatic: Why ask more?" Later Yang Min ran afoul of the law; people assumed Jiang Wan would let him hang."

sentences.zh: 琬心無適莫，得免重罪。

translations.literal: Wan’s heart had no favor or disdain; he obtained avoidance of heavy crime.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Wan bore him no grudge, and Yang Min escaped the gravest penalty."

sentences.zh: 其好惡存道，皆此類也。

translations.literal: His likes and dislikes preserving the Way were all of this sort.
translations.idiomatic: His sense of justice ran this way in every case."

sentences.zh: 琬以為昔諸葛亮數窺秦川，道險運艱，競不能克，不若乘水東下。

translations.literal: Wan thought that formerly Zhuge Liang several times spied on Qin River—the roads perilous and transport hard—and in the end could not overcome; better to ride the waters east.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Wan judged Zhuge Liang’s thrusts toward Qinchuan too costly; he preferred to strike east along the Han waters."

sentences.zh: 乃多作舟船，欲由漢、沔襲魏興、上庸。

translations.literal: Thereupon he built many boats and ships, intending by Han and Mian to raid Wei’s Xing and Shangyong.
translations.idiomatic: He built a fleet to sail down the Han and strike Wei’s Xingfang and Shangyong."

sentences.zh: 會舊疾連動，未時得行。

translations.literal: His old illness stirred in succession; he did not obtain timely march.
translations.idiomatic: Old illnesses flared and delayed the expedition."

sentences.zh: 而眾論鹹謂如不克捷，還路甚難，非長策也。

translations.literal: Yet crowd opinion all said if victory were not gained the return road would be very hard—not a long-term strategy.
translations.idiomatic: Court opinion warned that retreat would be perilous if the attack failed—a poor long-term plan."

sentences.zh: 於是遣尚書令費禕、中監軍姜維等喻指。

translations.literal: Thereupon he dispatched Masters of Writing chief Fei Yi and army inspector Jiang Wei and others to convey intent.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Fei Yi, Jiang Wei, and others to explain his reasoning to the court."

sentences.zh: 琬承命上疏曰：

translations.literal: Wan received the command and submitted memorial, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Wan then memorialized:

sentences.zh: 芟穢弭難，臣職是掌。

translations.literal: To cut weeds and settle troubles—my office holds that charge.
translations.idiomatic: Rooting out rebels and easing crises is the duty I bear.

sentences.zh: 自臣奉辭漢中，已經六年，臣既闇弱，加嬰疾疢，規方無成，夙夜憂慘。

translations.literal: Since I took leave from Hanzhong, six years have passed; I am dim and weak, moreover burdened by chronic illness—plans have achieved nothing; morning and night I am anxious and distressed.
translations.idiomatic: Six years have passed since I left Hanzhong; I am dull by nature and plagued by sickness, so my designs have come to nothing—I fret day and night.

sentences.zh: 今魏跨帶九州，根蒂滋蔓，平除未易。

translations.literal: Now Wei strides across nine provinces; roots and stems spread and creep—leveling them is not easy.
translations.idiomatic: Wei today spans the realm; its power runs deep—destroying it will not be swift.

sentences.zh: 若東西並力，首尾掎角。

translations.literal: If east and west exert strength together, head and tail like horns of a deer.
translations.idiomatic: If Shu and Wu strike together, we catch Wei between hammer and anvil.

sentences.zh: 雖未能速得如志，且當分裂蠶食，先摧其支黨。

translations.literal: Though we may not quickly obtain as wished, we ought yet to split and gnaw like silkworms, first crushing its limbs and parties.
translations.idiomatic: Even if total victory tarries, we can still gnaw at its borders and cut away its allies first.

sentences.zh: 然吳期二三，連不克果，俯仰惟艱，實忘寢食。

translations.literal: Yet Wu’s timing slips two or three times; repeatedly we cannot achieve fruit—looking up and down is only hardship; truly I forget sleep and food.
translations.idiomatic: Wu has missed joint deadlines again and again; every reversal tortures me—I hardly eat or sleep.

sentences.zh: 輒與費禕等議，以涼州胡塞之要，進退有資，賊之所惜；

translations.literal: Then with Fei Yi and others I judged that Liangzhou’s Hu frontier passes are critical—advance and retreat have resources—what the rebels cherish;
translations.idiomatic: Fei Yi and I concluded that Liangzhou’s frontier is vital ground—easy to supply and hard for Wei to abandon;

sentences.zh: 且羌、胡乃心思漢如渴。

translations.literal: moreover Qiang and Hu in heart long for Han like thirst.
translations.idiomatic: moreover Qiang and Hu tribes thirst for the Han cause.

sentences.zh: 又昔偏軍人羌，郭淮破走，算其長短，以為事首，宜以姜維為涼州刺史。

translations.literal: Also formerly the partial army entered the Qiang—Guo Huai was broken and fled—measuring strengths and weaknesses, taking this matter as foremost, Jiang Wei ought to be Liangzhou inspector.
translations.idiomatic: Our columns once pierced the Qiang lands and routed Guo Huai—weighing costs and gains, the first step is to name Jiang Wei Inspector of Liangzhou.

sentences.zh: 若維征行，銜持河右，臣當帥軍為維鎮繼。

translations.literal: If Wei campaigns, biting and holding the west of the river—I ought to lead an army as Wei’s rear support.
translations.idiomatic: When Jiang Wei advances to anchor the west of the Yellow River, I will follow with an army to sustain him.

sentences.zh: 今涪水陸四通，惟急是應。

translations.literal: Now Fu’s waterways and roads connect four ways—only urgency answers.
translations.idiomatic: Fu lies at a hub where land and water meet—we can rush reinforcements anywhere.

sentences.zh: 若東北有虞，赴之不難。

translations.literal: If the northeast has alarm, to hurry there is not hard.
translations.idiomatic: Should trouble flare in the northeast, relief can reach it quickly.

sentences.zh: 由是琬遂還住涪。

translations.literal: Thereby Wan then returned to dwell at Fu.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Wan therefore moved his headquarters back to Fu.

sentences.zh: 疾轉增劇，至九年卒，謚曰恭。

translations.literal: Illness turned and grew acute; in the ninth year he died, posthumous title Gong.
translations.idiomatic: His illness worsened; he died in the ninth year of Yanxi (246), posthumously titled Marquis Gong.

sentences.zh: 子斌嗣，為綏武將軍、漢城護軍。

translations.literal: Son Bin succeeded—general who pacifies martialness and protector of Han City.
translations.idiomatic: His son Jiang Bin inherited the rank as General Who Pacifies Might and Protector of Hanzhong.

sentences.zh: 魏大將軍鐘會至漢城，與斌書曰：「巴蜀賢智文武之士多矣，至於足下、諸葛思遠，譬諸草木，吾氣類也。

translations.literal: Wei grand general Zhong Hui reached Han City and wrote Bin, saying, "Ba–Shu wise and martial gentlemen are many—as for you and Zhuge Siyuan, compared to grass and trees, we are of one breath-class."
translations.idiomatic: When Zhong Hui’s army reached Hanzhong, he wrote Jiang Bin: "Shu is full of talent—yet you and Zhuge Zhan, like plants beside me, seem true kin."

sentences.zh: 桑梓之敬，古今所敦。

translations.literal: Respect for native place—ancient and modern esteem it.
translations.idiomatic: Revering a man’s home soil is a duty honored in every age."

sentences.zh: 西到，欲奉瞻尊大君公侯墓，當灑掃墳塋，奉祠致敬。

translations.literal: Westward I arrive and wish to pay respects at your noble fathers’ and lords’ tombs—I ought to sprinkle and sweep the burial mound and offer sacrifice with reverence.
translations.idiomatic: I am moving west and wish to sweep your fathers’ graves and leave offerings—pray tell me where they lie!"

sentences.zh: 願告其所在！

translations.literal: Wish you tell their location!
translations.idiomatic: Tell me where they rest!"

sentences.zh: 」斌答書曰：「知惟臭味意眷之隆，雅托通流，未拒來謂也。

translations.literal: " Bin answered in writing, saying, "I know only your warm regard and lofty intent—graciously you entrust flow and have not refused my coming address.
translations.idiomatic: " Jiang Bin replied: "I feel the kindness of your message and accept your friendly tone."

sentences.zh: 亡考昔遭疾疢，亡於涪縣，卜雲其吉，遂安厝之。

translations.literal: My late father long ago met illness and died in Fu County; divination said it was auspicious—thereupon we buried him securely.
translations.idiomatic: My father died of illness in Fu; the omens favored burial there, so he lies in that soil."

sentences.zh: 知君西邁，乃欲屈駕修敬墳墓。

translations.literal: Knowing you march west, you yet wish to humble your carriage to cultivate respect at the graves.
translations.idiomatic: Learning that you journey west to honor his tomb humbles me."

sentences.zh: 視予猶父，顏子之仁也，聞命感愴，以增情思。

translations.literal: To regard me as a father is the benevolence of Yan Hui—hearing the command I am moved and grieved, thereby increasing feeling and thought.
translations.idiomatic: You treat me like a son—this is kindness worthy of Yan Hui’s praise—your words stir deep emotion."

sentences.zh: 」會得斌書報，嘉歎意義，及至涪如其書雲。

translations.literal: " Hui received Bin’s letter reply, praised and sighed at the meaning; when he reached Fu it was as the letter said.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong Hui cherished the letter and, arriving at Fu, did exactly as promised.

sentences.zh: 後主既降鄧艾，斌詣會於涪，待以交友之禮。

translations.literal: After the Later Lord had surrendered to Deng Ai, Bin went to Hui at Fu; he treated him with the rites of friendship.
translations.idiomatic: After Liu Shan yielded to Deng Ai, Jiang Bin met Zhong Hui at Fu and was received as a friend.

sentences.zh: 隨會至成都，為亂兵所殺。

translations.literal: Following Hui to Chengdu, he was killed by mutinous troops.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Zhong Hui to Chengdu and died in the soldiers’ riot.

sentences.zh: 斌弟顯，為太子僕。

translations.literal: Bin’s younger brother Xian was crown prince’s steward.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Jiang Xian served as steward to the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 會亦愛其才學，與斌同時死。

translations.literal: Hui also loved his talent and learning; he died together with Bin.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong Hui admired his scholarship as well; he perished alongside Jiang Bin.

sentences.zh: 劉敏，左護軍、揚威將軍，與鎮北大將軍王平懼鎮漢巾。

translations.literal: Liu Min—Protector of the Left and General Who Displays Might—together with Grand General Who Guards the North Wang Ping jointly garrisoned Hanzhong (the chapter writes 巾 ‘scarf’ for 中 ‘middle’).
translations.idiomatic: Liu Min, General Who Displays Might and Protector of the Left, jointly held Hanzhong with Wang Ping (the text miswrites ‘scarf’ for ‘middle’).

sentences.zh: 魏遣大將軍曹爽襲蜀時，時議者或謂但可守城，不出拒敵，必自引退。

translations.literal: When Wei sent grand general Cao Shuang to raid Shu, debaters then said one could only defend the city and not go out to resist the enemy—they would surely withdraw of themselves.
translations.idiomatic: When Cao Shuang invaded, some urged staying behind walls—the enemy would retreat on their own.

sentences.zh: 敏以為男女布野，農谷棲畝，若聽敵人，則大事去矣。

translations.literal: Min thought men and women spread across the wilds, crops lodged in the furrows—if we listened to the enemy, the great affair would be lost.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Min argued that peasants and grain lay exposed in the fields—pure defense would surrender everything.

sentences.zh: 遂帥所領與平據興勢，多張旗幟，彌亙百餘里。

translations.literal: Thereupon he led those he commanded with Ping to hold Xingshi, spread many banners, stretching more than a hundred li.
translations.idiomatic: He marched with Wang Ping to Xingshi, planting banners along a hundred li of ridgeline.

sentences.zh: 會大將軍費禕從成都至，魏軍即退。

translations.literal: When grand general Fei Yi arrived from Chengdu, the Wei army at once withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: When Fei Yi brought reinforcements from Chengdu, the Wei army withdrew.

sentences.zh: 敏以功封雲亭侯。

translations.literal: Min for merit was enfeoffed marquis of Yun Village.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Min earned the village marquisate of Yun for this feat.

sentences.zh: 費禕字文偉，江夏鄳人也。

translations.literal: Fei Yi, courtesy name Wenwei, was a man of Mei in Jiangxia.
translations.idiomatic: Fei Yi, courtesy name Wenwei, came from Mei in Jiangxia.

sentences.zh: 〈鄳音盲。〉

translations.literal: < The graph Mei is read like ‘mang.’ >
translations.idiomatic: < Phonetic note: the place name Mei is pronounced like ‘mang.’ >

sentences.zh: 少孤，依族父伯仁。

translations.literal: In youth he was orphaned; he relied on his paternal uncle Boren.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned young, he was raised by his uncle Fei Boren.

sentences.zh: 伯仁姑，益州牧劉璋之母也。

translations.literal: Boren’s paternal aunt was the mother of provincial governor Liu Zhang.
translations.idiomatic: Fei Boren’s aunt was Liu Zhang’s mother.

sentences.zh: 璋遣使迎仁，仁將禕遊學入蜀。

translations.literal: Zhang sent envoys to welcome Boren; Boren took Yi to study abroad and enter Shu.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zhang summoned Boren, who brought the young Fei Yi to Shu to study.

sentences.zh: 會先主定蜀，禕遂留益土，與汝南許叔龍、南郡董允齊名。

translations.literal: As it happened the Vanguard Lord settled Yi; Yi thereupon remained in Yi soil, sharing fame with Xu Shulong of Runan and Dong Yun of Nan Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Bei took Yi Province, Fei Yi stayed on, winning equal renown with Xu Shulong and Dong Yun.

sentences.zh: 時許靖喪子，允與禕欲共會其葬所。

translations.literal: At the time Xu Jing had lost a son; Yun and Yi wished together to meet at his burial place.
translations.idiomatic: When Xu Jing’s son died, Dong Yun and Fei Yi meant to attend the funeral together.

sentences.zh: 允白父和請車，和遣開後鹿車給之。

translations.literal: Yun told father He to request a cart; He sent the rear-deer cart for them.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Yun asked his father Dong He for a vehicle; Dong He sent a one-ox cart from the household.

sentences.zh: 允有難載之色．禕便從前先上。

translations.literal: Yun had a hard-to-bear color of loading; Yi then went forward first and mounted.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Yun blushed at the humble cart, but Fei Yi climbed in without hesitation.

sentences.zh: 及於喪所，諸葛亮及諸貴人悉集，車乘甚鮮，允猶神色未泰，而禕晏然自若。

translations.literal: Arriving at the funeral site, Zhuge Liang and the various nobles all gathered; carriages and riders were very fresh—Yun’s expression was still not at ease, while Yi was calm and self-possessed.
translations.idiomatic: At the gathering Zhuge Liang and the notables arrived in fine carriages; Dong Yun looked ill at ease, but Fei Yi was perfectly composed.

sentences.zh: 持車人還，和問之，知其如此，乃謂允曰：「吾常疑汝於文偉優劣未別也。

translations.literal: When the cart man returned, He asked him, knew it was thus, and thereupon said to Yun, "I always doubted you and Wenwei’s superiority and inferiority were not yet distinguished.
translations.idiomatic: When the driver reported back, Dong He said to his son, "I used to wonder whether you or Fei Yi was the better man.

sentences.zh: 而今而後，吾意了矣。」

translations.literal: From now and after, my mind is clear."
translations.idiomatic: Now I know."

sentences.zh: 先主立太子，禕與允為舍人，遷庶子。

translations.literal: When the Vanguard Lord established the crown prince, Yi and Yun were attendants; he promoted them to junior mentors.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Bei named the crown prince and made Fei Yi and Dong Yun his attendants, later promoting them to junior mentors.

sentences.zh: 後主踐位，為黃門侍郎。

translations.literal: When the Later Lord ascended, he became gentleman of the Yellow Gates.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Shan took the throne, Fei Yi became a gentleman of the Yellow Gates.

sentences.zh: 丞相亮南征還，群僚於數十里逢迎，年位多在禕右，而亮特命禕同載，由是眾人莫不易觀。

translations.literal: When Chancellor Liang returned from the southern campaign, the host of officials met him at several tens of li—years and ranks were mostly to Yi’s right, yet Liang specially ordered Yi to ride in the same carriage; thereby everyone none did not change view.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhuge Liang returned from the south, officials welcomed him for miles; though many outranked Fei Yi, Zhuge Liang seated him in his own carriage—everyone suddenly saw him differently.

sentences.zh: 亮以初從南歸，以禕為昭信校尉使吳。

translations.literal: Liang because he had first returned from the south appointed Yi as colonel of shining trust and sent him to Wu.
translations.idiomatic: On that first return Zhuge Liang named Fei Yi Colonel of Shining Trust and sent him as envoy to Wu.

sentences.zh: 孫權性既滑稽，嘲啁無方，諸葛恪、羊誖等才博果辯，論難鋒至，禕辭順義篤，據理以答，終不能屈。

translations.literal: Sun Quan’s nature was moreover jesting—banter without rule—Zhuge Ke, Yang Zhuo and others were broadly learned and sharply eloquent; disputing difficulties pressed like blades—Yi’s words followed meaning firmly, answering by grasping principle; in the end they could not bend him.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan loved banter; Zhuge Ke and others pressed Fei Yi with sharp debate, but he answered calmly on principle and could not be cornered.

sentences.zh: 〈祎别传曰：孙权每别酌好酒以饮祎，视其已醉，然后问以国事，并论当世之务，辞难累至。

translations.literal: < Yi’s separate tradition says: Sun Quan each time separately poured fine wine to drink Yi, watched until he was drunk, then asked about state affairs and debated affairs of the age—hard questions piled up.
translations.idiomatic: < The supplemental biography states that Sun Quan plied Fei Yi with wine until he seemed drunk, then questioned him on state affairs—layer after layer of challenges.

sentences.zh: 祎辄辞以醉，退而撰次所问，事事条答，无所遗失。〉

translations.literal: Yi always declined on grounds of drunkenness, withdrew and composed in order what was asked—each matter answered in items, nothing lost.>
translations.idiomatic: Fei Yi pleaded drunkenness, went home, wrote out every question, and answered them point by point without omission.>

sentences.zh: 權甚器之，謂禕曰：「君天下淑德，必當股肱蜀朝，恐不能數來也。」

translations.literal: Quan greatly esteemed him and said to Yi, "You are the realm’s virtuous man—you must become pillar and thigh of the Shu court; I fear you cannot come often."
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan respected him deeply: "You are a paragon of virtue—you will anchor the Shu court; I doubt we shall see you often."

sentences.zh: 〈祎别传曰：权乃以手中常所执宝刀赠之，祎答曰：“臣以不才，何以堪明命？

translations.literal: < The supplemental biography says: Quan then with his own hand presented the precious knife he always carried; Yi answered, "I am without talent—how can I bear an enlightened command?
translations.idiomatic: < It adds that Sun Quan gave him his personal treasure sword; Fei Yi replied, "I lack ability—how could I accept such an honor?

sentences.zh: 然刀所以讨不庭、禁暴乱者也，但原大王勉建功业，同奖汉室，臣虽闇弱，终不负东顾。”〉

translations.literal: Yet a blade is what punishes those not courtly and restrains violence—I only wish the great king strive to build merit, together aid the House of Han; though I am dim and weak, in the end I will not betray the eastward gaze."
translations.idiomatic: Yet a sword is meant to chastise rebels—I pray you aid the Han house; though I am dull, I will not betray your trust looking eastward."

sentences.zh: 還，遷為侍中。

translations.literal: Returning, he was promoted to palace attendant.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he was promoted to palace attendant.

sentences.zh: 亮住北住漢中，請禕為參軍。

translations.literal: Liang dwelt north at Hanzhong and requested Yi as army adviser.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuge Liang garrisoned Hanzhong and appointed Fei Yi army adviser.

sentences.zh: 以奉使稱旨，頻煩至吳。

translations.literal: Because his mission matched intent, repeatedly he went to Wu.
translations.idiomatic: His missions pleased both courts, so he shuttled often to Wu.

sentences.zh: 建興八年，轉為中護軍，後又為司馬。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Jianxing he was transferred to protector of the army; afterward he became marshal.
translations.idiomatic: In Jianxing 8 (230) he became Protector of the Army, then marshal.

sentences.zh: 值軍師魏延與長史楊儀相憎惡。

translations.literal: It happened that army adviser Wei Yan and chief clerk Yang Yi mutually hated.
translations.idiomatic: Army Adviser Wei Yan and Chief Clerk Yang Yi hated each other bitterly.

sentences.zh: 每至並坐爭論，延或舉刀擬儀，儀泣涕橫集。

translations.literal: Whenever they sat together they argued; Yan sometimes raised a knife toward Yi; Yi wept and tears streamed.
translations.idiomatic: When they shared a tent Wei Yan threatened Yang Yi with his blade while Yang Yi wept.

sentences.zh: 禕常入其坐間，諫喻分別，終亮之世。

translations.literal: Yi often entered their seating space, remonstrating and distinguishing—throughout Liang’s lifetime.
translations.idiomatic: Fei Yi stepped between them with counsel for the rest of Zhuge Liang’s life.

sentences.zh: 各盡延、儀之用者，禕匡救之力也。

translations.literal: That each exhausted Yan and Yi’s usefulness was Yi’s power of rescue.
translations.idiomatic: That both men served their roles until Zhuge Liang died owed much to Fei Yi’s mediation.

sentences.zh: 亮卒，禕為後軍師。

translations.literal: When Liang died, Yi became rear army commander.
translations.idiomatic: After Zhuge Liang’s death Fei Yi became Rear Commander.

sentences.zh: 頃之，代蔣琬為尚書令。

translations.literal: Shortly he replaced Jiang Wan as Masters of Writing chief.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he succeeded Jiang Wan as Director of the Imperial Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 〈祎别传曰：于时军国多事，公务烦猥，祎识悟过人，每省读书记，举目暂视，已究其意旨，其速数倍於人，终亦不忘。

translations.literal: < The supplemental biography says: At that time army and state had many affairs; public business was vexatious and numerous—Yi’s perception surpassed others; each time he examined documents, lifting eyes briefly he already grasped their intent—his speed several times that of others—and in the end he also did not forget.
translations.idiomatic: < It notes that while military and civil business swamped the court, Fei Yi read memorials at a glance and forgot nothing.

sentences.zh: 常以朝晡听事，其间接纳宾客，饮食嬉戏，加之博弈，每尽人之欢，事亦不废。

translations.literal: He constantly heard morning and afternoon cases; in between he received guests—drink, food, games—and besides chess and weiqi—each time exhausting others’ pleasure—yet affairs were also not neglected.
translations.idiomatic: He held court mornings and afternoons, yet still feasted guests, played chess, and kept every document current.

sentences.zh: 董允代祎为尚书令，欲斅祎之所行，旬日之中，事多愆滞。

translations.literal: When Dong Yun succeeded Yi as Masters of Writing chief, he wished to imitate what Yi had practiced—within ten days many affairs were delayed and stuck.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Yun took Fei Yi’s place as Director but tried to copy his routine; within days the paperwork piled up.

sentences.zh: 允乃叹曰：“人才力相县若此甚远，此非吾之所及也。

translations.literal: Yun thereupon sighed, saying, "Men's talents and strengths hang apart thus far—this is not what I can reach.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Yun sighed: "The gap between his vigor and mine is immense—I cannot match him."

sentences.zh: 听事终日，犹有不暇尔。”〉

translations.literal: Hearing cases all day long, still there is what one cannot spare.
translations.idiomatic: Even listening to petitions from dawn to dusk I cannot finish everything."

sentences.zh: 琬自漢中還涪，禕遷大將軍，錄尚書事。

translations.literal: When Wan returned from Hanzhong to Fu, Yi was promoted grand general and recorded imperial secretariat affairs.
translations.idiomatic: After Jiang Wan withdrew from Hanzhong to Fu, Fei Yi became Grand General with supervisory authority over the secretariat.

sentences.zh: 延熙七年，魏軍次於興勢，假禕節，率眾往御之。

translations.literal: In Yanxi's seventh year Wei troops halted at Xingshi; Yi was lent credentials and led the host to oppose them.
translations.idiomatic: In Yanxi 7 (244), when Wei halted at Xingshi, Fei Yi took the imperial baton and marched to meet them.

sentences.zh: 光祿大夫來敏至禕許別，求共圍棋。

translations.literal: Minister Laimin came to Yi's quarters to bid farewell and requested to play weiqi together.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Mentor Lai Min visited Fei Yi before departure and challenged him to a game of weiqi.

sentences.zh: 於時羽檄交馳，人馬擐甲，嚴駕已訖。

translations.literal: At that time urgent bulletins flew crisscross; men and horses donned armor—strict readiness was already finished.
translations.idiomatic: Feather reports flew while troops stood harnessed and armed.

sentences.zh: 禕與敏留意對戲，色無厭倦。

translations.literal: Yi and Min attended closely to the match—his expression showed no disgust or weariness.
translations.idiomatic: Fei Yi gave the board his full attention without betraying anxiety.

sentences.zh: 敏曰：「向聊觀試君耳!君信可人，必能辦賊者也。

translations.literal: Min said, "Just now I idly tested you! You truly are the right man—you surely can manage the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Lai Min said: "I only tested you—you have the steel nerves needed against the enemy."

sentences.zh: 」禕至，敵遂退，封成鄉侯。

translations.literal: " When Yi arrived, the enemy then withdrew; he was enfeoffed marquis of Cheng Village.
translations.idiomatic: " Fei Yi reached the front and the Wei army withdrew; he received the village marquisate of Cheng.

sentences.zh: 〈殷基通语曰：司马懿诛曹爽，祎设甲乙论平其是非。

translations.literal: < Yin Ji's Comprehensive Tales records: When Sima Yi executed Cao Shuang, Yi drafted an A–B debate weighing their right and wrong.
translations.idiomatic: < Yin Ji records that after Sima Yi killed Cao Shuang, Fei Yi wrote an A-side/B-side essay debating the deed.

sentences.zh: 甲以为曹爽兄弟凡品庸人，苟以宗子枝属，得蒙顾命之任，而骄奢僭逸，交非其人，私树朋党，谋以乱国。

translations.literal: Side A held that Cao Shuang and his brothers were mediocre rustics—only because they were imperial kin did they receive testament authority—yet arrogance, luxury, and excess led them to trust unworthy men, build private factions, and plot to disorder the state.
translations.idiomatic: Side A: Cao Shuang’s faction were mediocre men lifted only by blood ties; they wasted power on favorites until treason loomed.

sentences.zh: 懿奋诛讨，一朝殄尽，此所以称其任，副士民之望也。

translations.literal: Yi rose to punish them—in one morning they were wiped out—thereby fulfilling his charge and answering scholar-officials' hopes.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Yi struck decisively and cleared them in a day—matching duty and popular expectation.

sentences.zh: 乙以为懿感曹仲付己不一，岂爽与相干？

translations.literal: Side B held that Yi resented Cao Shuang for inconsistent trust—how could Shuang alone cause trouble?
translations.idiomatic: Side B: Sima Yi nursed private resentment—Cao Shuang was not the sole culprit.

sentences.zh: 事势不专，以此阴成疵瑕。

translations.literal: Power was not concentrated—thereby he secretly bred faults.
translations.idiomatic: Shared authority let grudges fester unseen.

sentences.zh: 初无忠告侃尔之训，一朝屠戮，攙其不意，岂大人经国笃本之事乎！

translations.literal: From the first there was no earnest loyal counsel—yet in one dawn they slaughtered—catching them unaware—is that how great men anchor the state?
translations.idiomatic: He offered no warning, then slaughtered them overnight—hardly the steady hand of a chief minister.

sentences.zh: 若爽信有谋主之心，大逆已构，而发兵之日，更以芳委爽兄弟。

translations.literal: If Shuang truly harbored treason, great rebellion already framed—yet when troops marched he still entrusted Cao Fang to Shuang's brothers.
translations.idiomatic: If treason were real, why did he leave the emperor in Cao Shuang’s hands when mobilizing?

sentences.zh: 懿父子从后闭门举兵，蹙而向芳，必无悉宁，忠臣为君深虑之谓乎？

translations.literal: Yi and his son closed the gates behind and raised troops—pressing toward Fang—could loyal ministers deeply counsel thus?
translations.idiomatic: The Simas barred the palace and turned arms on the sovereign—was that loyal foresight?

sentences.zh: 以此推之，爽无大恶明矣。

translations.literal: By this reasoning Shuang had no great evil—it is clear.
translations.idiomatic: On this reading Cao Shuang’s guilt was hardly proven.

sentences.zh: 若懿以爽奢僭，废之刑之可也，灭其尺口，被以不义，绝子丹血食，及何晏子魏之亲甥，亦与同戮，为僭滥不当矣。〉

translations.literal: If Yi thought Shuang extravagant and presumptuous—depose or punish him—acceptable; but extinguishing his whole household, branding him unjust, cutting off Dan's sacrifices—and even executing He Yan, the emperor's kin—was cruel excess.>
translations.idiomatic: Executing the entire clan and collateral kin—including He Yan—went beyond justice.>

sentences.zh: 琬固讓州職，禕復領益州刺史。

translations.literal: Wan firmly yielded the provincial post; Yi again took Yi Province inspector.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Wan declined the governorship of Yi; Fei Yi reassumed it.

sentences.zh: 禕當國功名，略與琬比。

translations.literal: Yi holding state—merit and fame roughly matched Wan.
translations.idiomatic: As steward of Shu his stature rivaled Jiang Wan’s.

sentences.zh: 〈祎别传曰：祎雅性谦素，家不积财。

translations.literal: < The supplemental biography says: Yi was by nature humble and plain—his household did not hoard wealth.
translations.idiomatic: < It adds that Fei Yi lived modestly and kept little treasure.

sentences.zh: 兒子皆令布衣素食，出入不从车骑，无异凡人。〉

translations.literal: His sons were ordered plain cloth and vegetarian diet; going out they did not follow chariots and riders—no difference from common folk.>
translations.idiomatic: He made his sons dress like commoners and travel without escort.>

sentences.zh: 十一年，出住漢中，自琬及禕，雖自身在外，慶賞刑威，皆遙先咨斷然，後乃行。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he went out to garrison Hanzhong—from Wan and Yi onward, though themselves outside, rewards, punishments, and awe were all first consulted and decided from afar, then carried out.
translations.idiomatic: In Yanxi 11 (248) he moved to Hanzhong; even away from Chengdu he and Jiang Wan still settled rewards and punishments by courier before execution.

sentences.zh: 其推任如此。

translations.literal: Such was the trust placed in them.
translations.idiomatic: The court trusted them that completely.

sentences.zh: 後十四年夏，還成都，成都望氣者雲都邑無宰相位，故冬復比屯漢壽。

translations.literal: Later in the fourteenth year's summer he returned to Chengdu—Chengdu aura-readers said the capital lacked a minister's seat—therefore in winter he again camped north at Hanshou.
translations.idiomatic: Soothsayers claimed Chengdu held no seat for a chief minister, so he wintered again at Hanshou.

sentences.zh: 延熙十五年，命禕開府。

translations.literal: In Yanxi's fifteenth year he was ordered to open a general's office.
translations.idiomatic: In 252 he received authority to maintain a full general’s staff.

sentences.zh: 十六年歲首大會，魏降人郭循在坐。

translations.literal: At the new year great assembly of the sixteenth year, Wei defector Guo Xun sat among the guests.
translations.idiomatic: At the 253 New Year court, the Wei turncoat Guo Xiu was present.

sentences.zh: 禕歡飲沉醉，為循手刃所害，謚曰敬侯。

translations.literal: Yi drank merrily and sank drunk—Xun killed him with a hand blade—posthumous title Marquis Jing.
translations.idiomatic: Fei Yi drank himself senseless and Guo Xiu stabbed him; he was posthumously titled Marquis Jing.

sentences.zh: 子承嗣，為黃門侍郎，承弟恭，尚公主。

translations.literal: Son Cheng succeeded—as gentleman of Yellow Gates; Cheng's younger brother Gong married a princess.
translations.idiomatic: His son Fei Cheng became a Yellow Gates gentleman; younger brother Fei Gong married an imperial princess.

sentences.zh: 〈祎别传曰：恭为尚书郎，显名当世，早卒。〉

translations.literal: < The supplemental biography says: Gong was gentleman of the Masters of Writing—famed in his age—died early.>
translations.idiomatic: < It notes Fei Gong shone as a secretary but died young.>

sentences.zh: 禕長女配太子璿為妃。

translations.literal: Yi's eldest daughter was matched to crown prince Xuan as consort.
translations.idiomatic: Fei Yi’s eldest daughter became consort to Crown Prince Liu Xuan.

sentences.zh: 姜維，字伯約，天水冀人也。

translations.literal: Jiang Wei, courtesy name Boyue, was a man of Ji in Tianshui.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Wei, courtesy name Boyue, came from Ji in Tianshui.

sentences.zh: 少孤，與母居，好鄭氏學。

translations.literal: In youth orphaned, he dwelt with his mother and loved Zheng Xuan's learning.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned young, he lived with his mother and studied Zheng Xuan’s classical scholarship.

sentences.zh: 〈《傅子》曰：维为人好立功名，阴养死士，不脩布衣之业。〉

translations.literal: < The Fu Zi says: Wei by nature loved to establish merit and fame; secretly he nurtured braves and did not cultivate commoner's occupation.>
translations.idiomatic: < Fu Xuan claims Jiang Wei schemed for glory and kept a retinue of fighting men.>

sentences.zh: 仕郡上計掾，州闢為從事。

translations.literal: He served the commandery as accounts clerk; the province summoned him as attendant clerk.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to county accountant and then provincial attendant.

sentences.zh: 以父冏昔為郡功曹，值羌、戎叛亂，身衛郡將，沒於戰場，賜維官中郎，參本郡軍事。

translations.literal: Because father Jiong long ago was commandery merit clerk—when Qiang and Rong rebelled he guarded the prefect and died on the battlefield—Wei was granted gentleman cadet and joined his commandery's military staff.
translations.idiomatic: His father Jiang Jiong died defending the prefect against Qiang rebels; Jiang Wei received a cadet’s rank and a place on the staff.

sentences.zh: 建興六年，丞相諸葛亮軍向祁山，時天水太守適出案行。

translations.literal: In Jianxing's sixth year Chancellor Zhuge Liang's army aimed at Mount Qi—at that time Tianshui's prefect happened to be out inspecting.
translations.idiomatic: In 228 Zhuge Liang marched on Qi—Tianshui’s prefect was away on circuit.

sentences.zh: 維及功曹梁緒、主簿尹賞、主記梁虔等從行。

translations.literal: Wei together with merit clerk Liang Xu, chief clerk Yin Shang, recorder Liang Qian and others followed the circuit.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Wei rode with Liang Xu, Yin Shang, Liang Qian, and the staff.

sentences.zh: 太守聞蜀軍垂至而諸縣響應，疑維等皆有異心，於是夜亡保上邽。

translations.literal: The prefect heard Shu troops were near and counties were responding—suspected Wei and others all had alien hearts—thereupon fled by night to hold Shanggui.
translations.idiomatic: The prefect feared collaboration with Shu and fled overnight to Shanggui.

sentences.zh: 維等覺太守去，追遲，至城門，城門已閉，不納。

translations.literal: Wei and others noticed the prefect had gone—pursued late—reached the gate—the gate was closed—not admitted.
translations.idiomatic: They caught up too late; the city gates shut them out.

sentences.zh: 維等相率還冀，冀亦不入維。

translations.literal: Wei and others led one another back to Ji—Ji also would not admit Wei.
translations.idiomatic: They rode to Ji, but Ji refused them too.

sentences.zh: 維等乃俱詣諸葛亮。

translations.literal: Wei and others then all went to Zhuge Liang.
translations.idiomatic: They went together to Zhuge Liang.

sentences.zh: 會馬謖敗於街亭。

translations.literal: It happened Ma Su was defeated at Jieting.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Su had just been crushed at Jieting.

sentences.zh: 亮拔將西縣千餘家及維等還，故維遂與母相失。

translations.literal: Liang pulled west county thousand-plus households and Wei and others back—therefore Wei then lost contact with his mother.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuge Liang evacuated Xixian and brought Jiang Wei along—parting him from his mother.

sentences.zh: 〈《魏略》曰：天水太守马遵将维及诸官属随雍州刺史郭淮偶自西至洛门案行，会闻亮已到祁山，淮顾遵曰：“是欲不善！

translations.literal: < The Wei Lue says: Tianshui prefect Ma Zun led Wei and officials following provincial governor Guo Huai on circuit west to Luomen—happened to hear Liang had reached Qi Mountain—Huai looked at Zun and said, "This cannot be good!
translations.idiomatic: < The Wei Lue adds another flight from Tianshui: Ma Zun was west of Luomen with Guo Huai when news of Zhuge Liang arrived—Guo Huai cried trouble.

sentences.zh: ”遂驱东还上邽。

translations.literal: " Thereupon drove east back to Shanggui.
translations.idiomatic: " They galloped back toward Shanggui.

sentences.zh: 遵念所治冀县界在西偏，又恐吏民乐乱，遂亦随淮去。

translations.literal: Zun thought his jurisdiction Ji County lay on the west flank—also feared officials and people would delight in chaos—thereupon also followed Huai away.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Zun feared unrest in his western districts and fled with Guo Huai.

sentences.zh: 时维谓遵曰：“明府当还冀。

translations.literal: At the time Wei said to Zun, "My lord ought to return to Ji.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Wei urged Ma Zun to return and hold Ji.

sentences.zh: ”遵谓维等曰：“卿诸人

translations.literal: " Zun said to Wei and others, "You gentlemen—
translations.idiomatic: " Ma Zun told them, "You people—

translations.literal: (return)
translations.idiomatic: (text breaks mid-clause)

sentences.zh: 复信，皆贼也。

translations.literal: if you turn back again—all are bandits.
translations.idiomatic: —if you defect to the enemy you are traitors every one."

sentences.zh: ”各自行。

translations.literal: " Each went his own way.
translations.idiomatic: " Then each rode his separate path.

sentences.zh: 维亦无如遵何，而家在冀，遂与郡吏上官子脩等还冀。

translations.literal: Wei could do nothing about Zun—but his home was in Ji—thereupon with county clerk Shangguan Zixiu and others returned to Ji.
translations.idiomatic: Powerless to sway Ma Zun, Jiang Wei headed home to Ji with staff officer Shangguan Zixiu.

sentences.zh: 冀中吏民见维等大喜，便推令见亮。

translations.literal: Ji officials and people seeing Wei and others greatly rejoiced—and pushed them to go see Liang.
translations.idiomatic: The people of Ji welcomed them and urged them to meet Zhuge Liang.

sentences.zh: 二人不获已，乃共诣亮。

translations.literal: The two could not avoid it—thereupon together went to Liang.
translations.idiomatic: With little choice both men presented themselves to Zhuge Liang.

sentences.zh: 亮见，大悦。

translations.literal: Liang seeing them greatly rejoiced.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuge Liang received them gladly.

sentences.zh: 未及遣迎冀中人，会亮前锋为张郃、费繇等所破，遂将维等卻缩。

translations.literal: Before he could dispatch to welcome Ji people—it happened Liang's vanguard was broken by Zhang He, Fei Yao and others—thereupon led Wei and others to shrink back.
translations.idiomatic: Before Ji could be secured the vanguard fell to Zhang He—Zhuge Liang had to pull Jiang Wei back.

sentences.zh: 维不得还，遂入蜀。

translations.literal: Wei could not return—thereupon entered Shu.
translations.idiomatic: Cut off from Wei, Jiang Wei entered Shu.

sentences.zh: 诸军攻冀，皆得维母妻子，亦以维本无去意，故不没其家，但系保官以延之。

translations.literal: The various armies attacked Ji—all obtained Wei's mother and wife—also because Wei originally had no intent to leave—therefore did not confiscate his family—but tied them in protective custody to entice him.
translations.idiomatic: Wei besieged Ji and took his family but did not execute them, hoping to lure him back.

sentences.zh: 此语与本传不同。〉

translations.literal: This language differs from the main biography.>
translations.idiomatic: This variant differs from the standard account.>

sentences.zh: 亮辟維為倉曹掾，加奉義將軍，封當陽亭侯，時年二十七。

translations.literal: Liang summoned Wei as granary clerk; added general who upholds righteousness; enfeoffed village marquis of Dangyang—at the time age twenty-seven.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuge Liang made him Granary Clerk, General Who Upholds Righteousness, and Village Marquis of Dangyang—at twenty-seven.

sentences.zh: 亮與留府長史張裔、參軍蔣琬書曰：「姜伯約忠勤時事，思慮精密，考其所有，永南、季常諸人不如也。

translations.literal: Liang wrote to chief clerk Zhang Yi and adviser Jiang Wan: "Jiang Boyue is loyal and diligent in affairs of the time—thought careful and fine—measuring his qualities—Yongnan and Jichang and such do not match.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote Zhang Yi and Jiang Wan: "Jiang Wei is meticulous and loyal—Yongnan and Jichang cannot compare."

sentences.zh: 其人，涼州上士也。

translations.literal: This man is upper gentry of Liangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He is the finest talent of the northwest.

sentences.zh: 」又曰：「須先教中虎步兵五六千人。

translations.literal: " Also said: "Must first drill central tiger infantry five or six thousand.
translations.idiomatic: " Drill five or six thousand elite guards for him first.

sentences.zh: 姜伯約甚敏於軍事，既有膽義，深解兵意。

translations.literal: Jiang Boyue is very keen in military affairs—already has courage and duty—deeply understands soldier intent.
translations.idiomatic: He is bold in war and grasps how soldiers think.

sentences.zh: 此人心存漢室而才兼於人，畢教軍事，當遣詣宮，覲見主上。」

translations.literal: This man's heart cherishes the House of Han while talent surpasses others—when military teaching is finished—ought send him to palace—to gaze on the lord."
translations.idiomatic: His heart is Han’s—once trained, bring him to audience."

sentences.zh: 〈孙盛杂记曰：初，姜维诣亮，与母相失，复得母书，令求当归。

translations.literal: < Sun Sheng's Miscellany says: At first when Jiang Wei went to Liang he lost his mother—again obtained mother's letter ordering him to seek danggui medicine.
translations.idiomatic: < Sun Sheng adds that his mother wrote demanding he return.

sentences.zh: 维曰：“良田百顷，不在一亩，但有远志，不在当归也。”〉

translations.literal: Wei said: "A hundred qing of fine fields are not one acre—but one has yuanzhi medicine—not danggui."
translations.idiomatic: He answered with a pun: ‘far ambition,’ not ‘return home.’"

sentences.zh: 後遷中監軍、征西將軍。

translations.literal: Later promoted central army inspector and general who campaigns west.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Central Inspector and General Who Campaigns West.

sentences.zh: 十二年，亮卒，維還成都，為右監軍、輔漢將軍，統諸軍，進封平襄侯。

translations.literal: Twelfth year, Liang died; Wei returned Chengdu—became right army supervisor, assistant Han general—commanded various armies—advanced enfeoffment Pingxiang marquis.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year (234 CE), after Zhuge Liang died, Jiang Wei returned to Chengdu as right army supervisor and general who assists Han, commanding the hosts; he was advanced to marquis of Pingxiang.

sentences.zh: 延熙元年，隨大將軍蔣琬住漢中。

translations.literal: Yanxi first year, followed Grand General Jiang Wan dwelt Hanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: In Yanxi 1 he accompanied Grand General Jiang Wan to Hanzhong.

sentences.zh: 琬既遷大司馬。

translations.literal: Wan already transferred grand marshal.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Wan had by then become grand marshal.

sentences.zh: 以維為司馬，數率偏軍西入。

translations.literal: Used Wei as marshal—repeatedly led detached armies west entered.
translations.idiomatic: He made Jiang Wei his chief of staff, who repeatedly led flanking columns westward.

sentences.zh: 六年，遷鎮西大將軍，領涼州刺史。

translations.literal: Sixth year, promoted general who guards the west—concurrent Liangzhou inspector.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year (243 CE) he became general who guards the west with concurrent appointment as inspector of Liangzhou.

sentences.zh: 十年，遷衛將軍，與大將軍費禕共錄尚書事。

translations.literal: Tenth year, promoted general of the guards—together with Grand General Fei Yi jointly recorded masters affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year (247 CE) he became general of the guards and shared authority over the masters with Grand General Fei Yi.

sentences.zh: 是歲，漢山平康夷反，維率眾討定之。

translations.literal: This year, Hanshan Pingkang Yi rebelled—Wei led host attacked pacified them.
translations.idiomatic: That year the Pingkang Yi of Hanshan rebelled; Jiang Wei led troops and crushed them.

sentences.zh: 又出隴西、南安、金城界，與魏大將軍郭淮、夏侯霸等戰於洮西。

translations.literal: Again exited Longxi, Nan'an, Jincheng borders—with Wei grand general Guo Huai, Xiahou Ba etc. battled at Tao west.
translations.idiomatic: He campaigned through Longxi, Nan'an, and Jincheng and fought Wei generals Guo Huai and Xiahou Ba west of the Tao River.

sentences.zh: 胡王治無戴等舉部落降，維將還安處之。

translations.literal: Hu king Zhi Wudai etc. raised tribes submitted—Wei led returned peacefully settled them.
translations.idiomatic: The Qiang chieftain Zhi Wudai and his people surrendered; Jiang Wei escorted them back and settled them safely.

sentences.zh: 十二年，假維節復出西平，不克而還。

translations.literal: Twelfth year, lent Wei staff—again exited Xiping—not conquered but returned.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year (249 CE) Jiang Wei received credential staff and marched on Xiping again, failed to take it, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 維自以練西方風俗，兼負其才武，欲誘諸羌、胡以為羽翼，謂自隴以西可斷而有也。

translations.literal: Wei self thought practiced western customs—also bore his talent martial—wished entice various Qiang, Hu to become wings—said from Long westward could cut off and possess.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Wei knew the western frontier and trusted his skill at arms; he meant to win the Qiang and Hu as allies and carve out everything west of Long Mountain.

sentences.zh: 每欲興軍大舉，費禕常裁製不從，與其兵不過萬人。

translations.literal: Each time wished raise army great undertaking—Fei Yi constantly cut regulated not followed—gave him troops not exceeding ten thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he sought a major campaign Fei Yi checked him and sent fewer than ten thousand men.

sentences.zh: 〈《汉晋春秋》曰：费祎谓维曰：“吾等不如丞相亦已远矣；

translations.literal: 〈Han Jin Chunqiu says: Fei Yi spoke to Wei saying: "We not equal Chancellor also already far;
translations.idiomatic: The *Han Jin Chunqiu* records Fei Yi telling Jiang Wei, "We fall far short of the Chancellor;

sentences.zh: 丞相犹不能定中夏，况吾等乎！

translations.literal: Chancellor still could not settle central Xia—how much more us!
translations.idiomatic: even he could not pacify the Central Plains—how can we!

sentences.zh: 且不如保国治民，敬守社稷，如其功业，以俟能者，无以为希冀徼倖而决成败於一举。

translations.literal: Moreover not equal protect state govern people—reverently guard altars—as for such merit enterprise—wait able persons—do not think hope luck decide success defeat at one stroke.
translations.idiomatic: Better guard the realm and tend the people, honor the altars, leave grand achievement to worthier men—do not gamble everything on one reckless stroke."

sentences.zh: 若不如志，悔之无及。”〉

translations.literal: If not achieve intent—regret it without reaching."〉
translations.idiomatic: Fail and remorse will come too late."〉

sentences.zh: 十六年春，禕卒。

translations.literal: Spring of the sixteenth year—Yi died.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of 253 Fei Yi died.

sentences.zh: 夏，維率數萬人出石營，經董亭，圍南安。

translations.literal: Summer—Wei led several tens of thousands out Shiying—passed Dongting—besieged Nan'an.
translations.idiomatic: That summer Jiang Wei marched from Shiying through Dongting to besiege Nan'an.

sentences.zh: 魏雍州刺史陳泰解圍至洛門，維糧盡退還。

translations.literal: Wei Yongzhou inspector Chen Tai relieved the siege reaching Luomen—Wei grain exhausted and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Tai relieved Nan'an at Luomen; Jiang Wei ran out of supplies and retreated.

sentences.zh: 明年，加督中外軍事。

translations.literal: Next year added supervisor of inner and outer military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he gained overall military command.

sentences.zh: 復出隴西，守狄道長李簡舉城降。

translations.literal: Again exited Longxi—Didao chief Li Jian raised the city to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: He struck Longxi again; Li Jian of Didao surrendered the town.

sentences.zh: 進圍襄武，與魏將徐質交鋒，斬首破敵，魏軍敗退。

translations.literal: Advanced to besiege Xiangwu—crossed spears with Wei general Xu Zhi—beheaded and broke the enemy—Wei army defeated and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: At Xiangwu he crushed Xu Zhi and drove Wei back.

sentences.zh: 維乘勝多所降下，拔河間狄道、臨洮三縣民還。

translations.literal: Wei rode victory—many surrendered—pulled Hejian Didao and Lintao three counties' people back.
translations.idiomatic: He followed up with evacuating river-district residents from Didao and Lintao.

sentences.zh: 後十八年，復與車騎將軍夏侯霸等俱出狄道，大破魏雍州刺史王經於洮西，經眾死者數萬人。

translations.literal: Later eighteenth year—again with general of chariots Xiahou Ba and others all exited Didao—greatly defeated Wei Yongzhou inspector Wang Jing west of the Tao—Jing's host dead numbered tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: In 255 he and Xiahou Ba smashed Wang Jing’s army on the Tao—tens of thousands fell.

sentences.zh: 經退保狄道城，維圍之。

translations.literal: Jing retreated to protect Didao city—Wei besieged it.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jing fled into Didao; Jiang Wei besieged him.

sentences.zh: 魏徵西將軍陳泰進兵解圍，維卻住鐘題。

translations.literal: Wei general who campaigns west Chen Tai advanced troops to relieve siege—Wei drew back to Zhongti.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Tai lifted the siege; Jiang Wei withdrew to Zhongti.

sentences.zh: 十九年春，就遷維為大將軍。

translations.literal: Spring of nineteenth year—then promoted Wei grand general.
translations.idiomatic: In 256 spring he became Grand General.

sentences.zh: 更整勒戎馬，與鎮西大將軍胡濟期會上邽。

translations.literal: Again arrayed horses—joined grand general who guards west Hu Ji—appointed rendezvous at Shanggui.
translations.idiomatic: He mustered troops to meet Hu Ji at Shanggui.

sentences.zh: 濟失誓不至，故維為魏大將鄧艾所破於段谷，星散流離，死者甚眾。

translations.literal: Ji broke oath and did not arrive—therefore Wei was by Wei grand general Deng Ai defeated at Duangu—scattered like stars and roaming—dead very many.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Ji failed to appear; Deng Ai routed Jiang Wei at Duangu with heavy losses.

sentences.zh: 眾庶由是怨讟，而隴已西亦騷動不寧。

translations.literal: The multitude thereby murmured blame—and west of Long also stirred restless.
translations.idiomatic: Soldiers cursed him and Longxi grew restless.

sentences.zh: 維謝過引負，求自貶削。

translations.literal: Wei apologized fault and bore blame—requested self-demotion.
translations.idiomatic: He owned the defeat and asked to be stripped of rank.

sentences.zh: 為後將軍，行大將軍事。

translations.literal: Made rear general—acting grand general affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Rear General while conducting Grand General business.

sentences.zh: 二十年，魏徵東大將軍諸葛誕反於淮南，分關中兵東下。

translations.literal: Twentieth year, Wei eastern campaign grand general Zhuge Dan rebelled at Huainan—divided Guanzhong troops east descended.
translations.idiomatic: In the twentieth year (257 CE) Wei's eastern campaign general Zhuge Dan rebelled in Huainan; Wei stripped Guanzhong to march east.

sentences.zh: 維欲乘虛向秦川，復率數萬人出駱谷，逕至沈嶺。

translations.literal: Wei wished ride emptiness toward Qin plain—again led several tens thousand exited Luogu valley—straight arrived Shen ridge.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Wei meant to exploit the gap toward Qinchuan; he led tens of thousands through Luogu Valley straight to Shen Ridge.

sentences.zh: 時長城積穀甚多而守兵乃少，聞維方到眾皆惶懼。

translations.literal: At time Changcheng piled grain very much yet guard troops few—heard Wei just arrived—crowd all fearful afraid.
translations.idiomatic: Changcheng held huge grain stores but few defenders; when Jiang Wei arrived they panicked.

sentences.zh: 魏大將軍司馬望拒之，鄧艾亦自隴右，皆軍於長城。

translations.literal: Wei grand general Sima Wang resisted him—Deng Ai also from Long right—all army at Changcheng.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Grand General Sima Wang blocked him; Deng Ai came from Longyou—both camped at Changcheng.

sentences.zh: 維前住芒水，皆倚山為營。

translations.literal: Wei advanced dwelt Mang River—all leaned mountain made camps.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Wei advanced to the Mang River and entrenched along the hills.

sentences.zh: 望、艾傍渭堅圍，維數下挑戰，望、艾不應。

translations.literal: Wang, Ai beside Wei firmly surrounded—Wei repeatedly descended challenged—Wang, Ai did not respond.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Wang and Deng Ai hugged the Wei River in tight defense; Jiang Wei challenged again and again—they refused battle.

sentences.zh: 景耀元年，維聞誕破敗，乃還成都。

translations.literal: Jingyao first year, Wei heard Dan defeated destroyed—then returned Chengdu.
translations.idiomatic: In Jingyao 1 (258 CE), hearing Zhuge Dan had fallen, Jiang Wei withdrew to Chengdu.

sentences.zh: 復拜大將軍。

translations.literal: Again appointed grand general.
translations.idiomatic: He was again appointed grand general.

sentences.zh: 初，先主留魏延鎮漢中，皆實兵諸圍以御外敵。

translations.literal: Formerly the Vanguard Lord left Wei Yan to hold Hanzhong—all filled soldiers at various ramparts to resist outer foes.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Bei left Wei Yan in Hanzhong with strong garrisons on every pass.

sentences.zh: 敵若來攻，使不得人。

translations.literal: If enemy came to attack—make them unable to enter.
translations.idiomatic: The aim was to stop invaders at the mountains.

sentences.zh: 及興勢之役，王平捍拒曹爽，皆承此制。

translations.literal: Down to Xingshi campaign—Wang Ping resisted Cao Shuang—all inherited this system.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Ping followed the same layered defense at Xingshi.

sentences.zh: 維建議，以為錯守諸圍，雖合《周易》「重門」之義，然適可禦敵，不獲大利。

translations.literal: Wei proposed opinion—thought guarding scattered ramparts—although matching Zhouyi ‘layered gates’ meaning—yet only able to ward enemy—not obtain great profit.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Wei argued that scattered stockades, though like the Yijing’s ‘double gates,’ only ward off raids without winning decisive gains.

sentences.zh: 不若使聞敵至，諸圍皆斂兵聚谷，退就漢、樂二城。

translations.literal: Better let hearing enemy arrive—all ramparts gather troops and grain—withdraw to Han and Le two cities.
translations.idiomatic: Better to concentrate grain and men in Hanxing and Lecheng when enemies approach.

sentences.zh: 使敵不得入平，臣重關鎮守以捍之。

translations.literal: Make enemy unable to enter the plain—I heavy gates defend to resist.
translations.idiomatic: Seal the exits so Wei cannot pour onto the plain.

sentences.zh: 有事之日，令遊軍並進以伺其虛。

translations.literal: When affair rises—order roaming troops advance together to spy their emptiness.
translations.idiomatic: Send mobile columns to strike any gap.

sentences.zh: 敵攻關不克，野無散谷，千里縣糧，自然疲乏。

translations.literal: Enemy attacks passes without overcoming—wilds lack scattered grain—thousand li hanging grain—naturally weary.
translations.idiomatic: If they cannot storm the passes they starve on long supply lines.

sentences.zh: 引退之日，然後諸城並出，與遊軍並力搏之，此殄敵之術也。

translations.literal: When they draw back—then all cities issue forth together—with roaming troops jointly strike—this is art of exterminating enemy.
translations.idiomatic: When they retreat, sally from every fort—annihilation tactics.

sentences.zh: 於是令督漢中胡濟卻住漢壽，監軍王含守樂城，護軍蔣斌守漢城，又於西安、建威、武衛、石門、武城、建昌、臨遠皆立圍守。

translations.literal: Thereupon ordered supervisor of Hanzhong Hu Ji to withdraw to Hanshou—army overseer Wang Han guards Le city—protector Jiang Bin guards Han city—and at Xi'an, Jianwei, Wuwei, Shimen, Wucheng, Jianchang, Linyuan all established rampart guards.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Ji pulled back to Hanshou; Wang Han held Lecheng; Jiang Bin held Hanxing; new posts ringed the frontier.

sentences.zh: 五年，維率眾出漢。

translations.literal: Fifth year—Wei led the host out from Han.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of the Jingyao era (262) he led the army out from Hanzhong.

sentences.zh: 侯和為鄧艾所破，還住沓中。

translations.literal: He was defeated at Hehe by Deng Ai and withdrew to garrison Tazhong.
translations.idiomatic: Deng Ai scattered him at Hehe; Jiang Wei fell back to Tazhong.

sentences.zh: 維本羈旅托國，累年攻戰，功績不立。

translations.literal: Wei was by nature a wanderer relying on the state—year after year attacking yet merit not established.
translations.idiomatic: A northerner serving Shu, he campaigned endlessly with little to show for it.

sentences.zh: 而宦官黃皓等弄權於內，右大將軍閻宇與皓協比，而皓陰欲廢維樹宇。

translations.literal: Yet eunuch Huang Hao and others wielded power within; General of the Right Yan Yu colluded with Hao—and Hao secretly wished to dismiss Wei and raise Yu.
translations.idiomatic: Court eunuch Huang Hao meddled at court; Yan Yu curried favor with him while Huang schemed to replace Jiang Wei.

sentences.zh: 維亦疑之，故自危懼，不復還成都。

translations.literal: Wei also suspected this—therefore lived in peril fear—no longer returned to Chengdu.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Wei feared court intrigue and stayed away from Chengdu.

sentences.zh: 〈《华阳国志》曰；

translations.literal: < The Huayang Guo Zhi records:
translations.idiomatic: < The Huayang Guo Zhi relates:

sentences.zh: 维恶黄皓恣擅，启后主欲杀之。

translations.literal: Wei detested Huang Hao's wantonness and memorialized the Later Lord wishing to kill him.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Wei denounced Huang Hao’s excess and asked Liu Shan to execute him.

sentences.zh: 后主曰：“皓趋走小臣耳，往董允切齿，吾常恨之，君何足介意！

translations.literal: The Later Lord said, "Hao is only a running petty minister—long ago Dong Yun gnashed teeth at him—I always resented that—why should you care!"
translations.idiomatic: Liu Shan dismissed him: "Huang Hao is a mere runner—Dong Yun hated him too, yet I kept him—why fuss?"

sentences.zh: ”维见皓枝附叶连，惧於失言，逊辞而出。

translations.literal: " Wei saw Hao's branches attached leaves connected—feared misspeaking—yielding words and departed.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing Huang Hao’s network, Jiang Wei held his tongue and withdrew politely.

sentences.zh: 后主敕皓诣维陈谢。

translations.literal: The Later Lord ordered Hao to go to Wei and declare apology.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Shan sent Huang Hao to apologize to Jiang Wei.

sentences.zh: 维说皓求沓中种麦，以避内逼耳。〉

translations.literal: Wei persuaded Hao to seek wheat planting at Tazhong—to avoid inner pressure.>
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Wei asked leave to grow grain at Tazhong and escape court cabals.>

sentences.zh: 六年，維表後主：「聞鐘會治兵關中，欲規進取，宜並遣張翼、廖化詣督堵軍分護陽安關口、陰平橋頭，以防未然。

translations.literal: Sixth year—Wei memorialized the Later Lord: "I hear Zhong Hui trains troops in Guanzhong—intends to strike—we ought together dispatch Zhang Yi and Liao Hua to various supervisors to divide guard Yang'an pass and Yinping bridge—to guard before it happens."
translations.idiomatic: In 263 he urged Liu Shan: Zhong Hui is mustering in Guanzhong—send Zhang Yi and Liao Hua to bolt Yang’an Pass and Yinping Bridge before it is too late.

sentences.zh: 」皓徵信鬼巫，謂敌終不自致。

translations.literal: " Hao trusted ghost shamans—said the enemy in the end would not come of themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Hao trusted sorcerers who swore the enemy would never march.

sentences.zh: 啟後主寢其事，而群臣不知。

translations.literal: He had the Later Lord sleep on the matter—and the host of ministers knew not.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Shan buried the memorial; the court never heard of it.

sentences.zh: 及鐘會將向駱谷，鄧艾將入沓中。

translations.literal: By the time Zhong Hui was bound for Lu Valley and Deng Ai for Tazhong—
translations.idiomatic: When Zhong Hui entered Lu Valley and Deng Ai struck Tazhong,

sentences.zh: 然後乃遣右車騎廖化詣沓中為維援，左車騎張翼、輔國大將軍董厥等詣陽安關口以為諸圍外助。

translations.literal: only then sent General of the Right Cavalry Liao Hua to Tazhong as aid to Wei—General of the Left Cavalry Zhang Yi and Defender-in-Chief Dong Jue and others to Yang'an pass as outer help for the ramparts.
translations.idiomatic: relief came late: Liao Hua toward Tazhong, Zhang Yi and Dong Jue toward Yang’an.

sentences.zh: 比至陰平，聞魏將諸葛緒向建威，故住待之。

translations.literal: Reaching Yinping—heard Wei general Zhuge Xu was heading for Jianwei—therefore halted to await.
translations.idiomatic: At Yinping he learned Zhuge Xu was aiming at Jianwei and paused.

sentences.zh: 月餘，維為鄧艾所摧，還住陰平。

translations.literal: After more than a month—Wei was crushed by Deng Ai—withdrew to Yinping.
translations.idiomatic: A month later Deng Ai broke him and he fell back to Yinping.

sentences.zh: 鐘會攻圍漢、樂二城，遣別將進攻關口，蔣舒開城出降，傅僉格鬥而死。

translations.literal: Zhong Hui attacked and besieged Han and Le two cities—sent a separate general to advance on the pass—Jiang Shu opened the city to surrender—Fu Qian wrestled and died.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong Hui stormed Hanxing and Lecheng and sent a column at the pass—Jiang Shu surrendered while Fu Qian died fighting.

sentences.zh: 〈汉晋春秋曰：蒋舒将出降，乃诡谓傅佥曰：“今贼至不击而闭城自守，非良图也。

translations.literal: < The Han–Jin Annals says: Jiang Shu was about to surrender—deceitfully said to Fu Qian, "Now the bandits arrive—not striking yet closing the city to self-defend—is not a good plan.
translations.idiomatic: < The Han–Jin Annals: Jiang Shu meant to defect and lied to Fu Qian: "Holding the gates without fighting helps no one."

sentences.zh: ”佥曰：“受命保城，惟全为功，今违命出战，若丧师负国，死无益矣。

translations.literal: " Qian said, "Ordered to guard the city—only completeness is merit—now disobeying order to go out—if we lose the army and betray the state—death is without benefit.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Qian answered: "Our orders are to hold—sortie risks defeat and dishonors the realm."

sentences.zh: ”舒曰：“子以保城获全为功，我以出战克敌为功，请各行其志。

translations.literal: " Shu said, "You take guarding the city and achieving completeness as merit—I take going out and defeating the enemy as merit—pray each walk his will.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Shu said: "You call defense victory—I call a sortie victory—do as you believe."

sentences.zh: ”遂率众出。

translations.literal: " Thereupon led the host out.
translations.idiomatic: Then he marched out with his men.

sentences.zh: 佥谓其战也，至阴平，以降胡烈。

translations.literal: Qian thought he went to battle—reaching Yinping—surrendered to Hu Lie.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Qian thought it a real attack; Jiang Shu slipped to Yinping and surrendered to Hu Lie.

sentences.zh: 烈乘虚袭城，佥格斗而死，魏人义之。

translations.literal: Lie rode emptiness to raid the city—Qian wrestled and died—Wei men deemed him righteous.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Lie seized the open gate; Fu Qian fought to the death and earned Wei’s respect.

sentences.zh: 蜀记曰：蒋舒为武兴督，在事无称。

translations.literal: Shu Ji says: Jiang Shu was overseer of Wuxing—without distinction in office.
translations.idiomatic: The Shu Ji adds that Jiang Shu had performed poorly as Wuxing commander.

sentences.zh: 蜀命人代之，因留舒助汉中守。

translations.literal: Shu ordered a man to replace him—thereupon retained Shu to assist Hanzhong defense.
translations.idiomatic: Shu replaced him but kept him to help defend Hanzhong.

sentences.zh: 舒恨，故开城出降。〉

translations.literal: Shu resented—therefore opened the city to surrender.>
translations.idiomatic: Bitter at the snub, Jiang Shu opened the gates to the enemy.>

sentences.zh: 會攻樂城，不能克。

translations.literal: Hui attacked Le city—could not overcome.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong Hui failed to storm Lecheng.

sentences.zh: 聞關口已下，長驅而前，翼、厥甫至漢壽，維、化亦捨陰平而退。

translations.literal: Hearing the pass had fallen—long drove forward—Yi, Jue had just reached Hanshou—Wei, Hua also abandoned Yinping and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: When the pass fell Zhong Hui drove deep; Zhang Yi and Dong Jue had only reached Hanshou while Jiang Wei and Liao Hua quit Yinping.

sentences.zh: 適與翼、厥合，皆退保劍閣以拒會。

translations.literal: Happening to join Yi, Jue—all retreated to guard Jiange to resist Hui.
translations.idiomatic: They united at Jiange and blocked Zhong Hui.

sentences.zh: 會與維書曰：「公侯以文武之德，懷邁世之略，功濟巴、漢、聲暢華夏，遠近莫不歸名。

translations.literal: Hui wrote Wei a letter, saying, "Lordship with civil and martial virtue—embracing transcendent age strategy—merit bridges Ba and Han—fame rings Huaxia—far and near none do not submit name.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong Hui flattered Jiang Wei: your virtue shakes Ba and Han and every corner defers to you.

sentences.zh: 每惟疇昔，嘗同大化，吳札、鄭喬，能喻斯好。

translations.literal: Each thinks on past days—once shared great transformation—Wu Zha, Zheng Qiao—can illustrate this friendship.
translations.idiomatic: He likened their tie to the cordial respect of ancient worthies.

sentences.zh: 」維不答書，列營守險。

translations.literal: " Wei did not answer the letter—arrayed camps guarding the defile.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Wei ignored the letter and manned the narrows.

sentences.zh: 會不能克，糧運縣遠，將議還歸。

translations.literal: Hui could not overcome—grain transport hung far—generals debated returning.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong Hui stalled; supplies stretched thin and withdrawal loomed.

sentences.zh: 而鄧艾自陰平由景谷道傍入，遂破諸葛瞻於綿竹。

translations.literal: Yet Deng Ai from Yinping by Jinggu side path slipped in—thereupon broke Zhuge Zhan at Mianzhu.
translations.idiomatic: Deng Ai cut through Yinping’s side valley and crushed Zhuge Zhan at Mianzhu.

sentences.zh: 後主請降於艾，艾前據成都。

translations.literal: The Later Lord requested surrender to Ai—Ai advanced and occupied Chengdu.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Shan surrendered to Deng Ai, who marched into Chengdu.

sentences.zh: 維等初聞瞻破，或聞後主欲固守成都，或聞欲東入吳，或聞欲南人建寧。

translations.literal: Wei and others first heard Zhan broken—or heard the Later Lord wished to firm defend Chengdu—or heard wished to east enter Wu—or heard wished to south enter Jianning.
translations.idiomatic: Rumors flew: Liu Shan might hold Chengdu, flee to Wu, or bolt south to Jianning.

sentences.zh: 於是引軍由廣漢、郪道以審虛實。

translations.literal: Thereupon led army by Guanghan, Qishan road—to examine emptiness and substance.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Wei marched through Guanghan toward Qi to learn the truth.

sentences.zh: 尋被後主敕令乃投戈放甲，詣會於涪軍前，將士鹹怒，拔刀斫石。

translations.literal: Soon received Later Lord order—then cast aside weapons, loosened armor—went to Hui before Fu army—generals all angry—drew blades and hacked stone.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Shan’s order to disarm reached him at Fu; his troops wept and struck rocks with their swords.

sentences.zh: 〈干宝《晋纪》云：会谓维曰；

translations.literal: < Gan Bao's Jin Ji records: Hui said to Wei—
translations.idiomatic: < Gan Bao’s Jin Annals: Zhong Hui asked Jiang Wei—

sentences.zh: “来何迟也？

translations.literal: "Why did you come so late?
translations.idiomatic: "Why so late?"

sentences.zh: ”维正色流涕曰：“今日见此为速矣！

translations.literal: " Wei with stern color weeping said, "Today to see this—is already swift!
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Wei answered through tears: "To meet this moment is soon enough!"

sentences.zh: ”会甚奇之。〉

translations.literal: " Hui greatly marveled.>
translations.idiomatic: Zhong Hui marveled at him.>

sentences.zh: 會厚待維等，皆權還其印號節蓋。

translations.literal: Hui thickly treated Wei and others—all temporarily returned their seals, tallies, and parasols.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong Hui honored Jiang Wei’s staff and returned their credentials.

sentences.zh: 會與維出則同輿，坐則同席，謂長史杜預曰：「以伯約比中土名士，公休、太初不能勝也。」

translations.literal: Hui with Wei—going out then same carriage—sitting then same mat—said to chief clerk Du Yu, "Comparing Boyue to central land famous scholars—Gongxiu, Taichu cannot surpass."
translations.idiomatic: He rode and sat with Jiang Wei and told Du Yu that Jiang Wei outshone elite Wei scholars.

sentences.zh: 〈《世语》曰：时蜀官属皆天下英俊，无出维右。〉

translations.literal: < The Shiyu says: At that time Shu officials were all the realm’s heroes—none exceeded Wei’s right.>
translations.idiomatic: < The Shiyu records that no Shu minister surpassed Jiang Wei.>

sentences.zh: 會既構鄧艾，艾檻車征，因將維等詣成都，自稱益州牧以叛。

translations.literal: Hui having framed Deng Ai—Ai in caged cart summoned—thereupon led Wei and others to Chengdu—self-proclaimed Yi Province shepherd in rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong Hui destroyed Deng Ai, hauled him east in a cage, marched on Chengdu with Jiang Wei, and styled himself governor of Yi with rebellious intent.

sentences.zh: 〈○《汉晋春秋》曰：会阴怀异图，维见而知其心，谓可构成扰乱以图克复也，乃诡说会曰：“闻君自淮南已来，算无遗策，晋道克昌，皆君之力。

translations.literal: < The Han–Jin Annals records: Hui secretly harbored alien plans—Wei saw and knew his heart—thought could weave disturbance to restore—thereupon deceitfully persuaded Hui, saying, "Hearing you from Huainan hither—calculations without slip—Jin way prospers—all your strength.
translations.idiomatic: < The Annals: Jiang Wei read Zhong Hui’s treason and flattered him: your campaigns since Huainan never fail.

sentences.zh: 今复定蜀，威德振世，民高其功，主畏其谋，欲以此安归乎！

translations.literal: Now again settling Shu—awe and virtue shake the age—people exalt your merit—lord fears your strategy—wish by this to peaceful return?
translations.idiomatic: You have conquered Shu—your fame terrifies Luoyang; can you simply go home in peace?

sentences.zh: 夫韩信不背汉於扰攘，以见疑於既平，大夫种不从范蠡於五湖，卒伏剑而妄死，彼岂闇主愚臣哉？

translations.literal: Husband Xin did not betray Han in turmoil—yet was suspected when peace came—great minister Chong did not follow Fan Li on Five Lakes—ultimately fell on sword in vain death—were those dull lords and foolish ministers?
translations.idiomatic: Han Xin and Wen Zhong fell once peace came—fortune and peril force such ends.

sentences.zh: 利害使之然也。

translations.literal: Profit and harm made it thus.
translations.idiomatic: Power twists fate so.

sentences.zh: 今君大功既立，大德已著，何不法陶硃公泛舟绝迹，全功保身，登峨嵋之岭，而从赤松游乎？

translations.literal: Now lord great merit already established—great virtue already manifest—why not emulate Tao Zhu Gong boating to vanish trace—complete merit and protect body—ascend Emei’s ridge—and follow Chisongzi roaming?
translations.idiomatic: Why not sail away like Fan Li while glory lasts and save your skin?

sentences.zh: ”会曰：“君言远矣，我不能行，且为今之道，或未尽於此也。
