translations.literal: " Hui said, "Your words are distant—I cannot practice—and as for present path—or not yet exhausted here.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong Hui called the advice impractical for him.

sentences.zh: ”维曰：“其他则君智力之所能，无烦於老夫矣。

translations.literal: " Wei said, "As for the rest—lord's intelligence and strength can reach—no bother this old man.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Wei said: "Leave the rest to you—I need not counsel that."

sentences.zh: ”由是情好欢甚。

translations.literal: " Thereby affection and friendship greatly joyous.
translations.idiomatic: They grew intimate.

sentences.zh: ○《华阳国志》曰：维教会诛北来诸将，既死，徐欲杀会，尽坑魏兵，还复蜀祚，密书与后主曰：“原陛下忍数日之辱，臣欲使社稷危而复安，日月幽而复明。

translations.literal: ○ The Huayang Guo Zhi records: Wei taught Hui to execute northern generals—after dead—gradually wished to kill Hui—bury all Wei soldiers—return restore Shu reign—secret letter to Later Lord said, "Wish your majesty endure days of shame—your servant wishes make altars of soil and grain dangerous again peace—sun and moon dark again bright.
translations.idiomatic: The Huayang Guo Zhi says Jiang Wei urged Zhong Hui to purge Wei officers, then wrote Liu Shan secretly promising to restore Shu.

sentences.zh: ”○孙盛《晋阳秋》曰：盛以永和初从安西将军平蜀，见诸故老，及姜维既降之后密与刘禅表疏，说欲伪服事锺会，因杀之以复蜀土，会事不捷，遂至泯灭，蜀人於今伤之。

translations.literal: " ○ Sun Sheng's Jin Yangqiu records: Sheng in Yonghe early followed Grand General West pacifying Shu—saw various elders—and Jiang Wei after surrendering secretly memorialized Liu Shan—said wished falsely serve Zhong Hui—thereby kill him to restore Shu soil—Hui affair did not succeed—thereupon reached extinction—Shu people to now mourn.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Sheng, visiting Shu in Yonghe, heard elders mourn Jiang Wei’s failed plot to kill Zhong Hui.

sentences.zh: 盛以为古人云，非所困而困焉名必辱，非所据而据焉身必危，既辱且危，死其将至，其姜维之谓乎！

translations.literal: Sheng thought ancient people said—what is not trapped yet trapped—name must shame—what is not relied on yet relied—body must danger—already shame and danger—death its will arrive—is this speaking of Jiang Wei!
translations.idiomatic: Sun Sheng cited the Yijing: Jiang Wei courted ruin by overreaching.

sentences.zh: 邓艾之入江由，士众鲜少，维进不能奋节绵竹之下，退不能总帅五将，拥卫蜀主，思后图之计，而乃反覆於逆顺之间，希违情於难冀之会，以衰弱之国，而屡观兵於三秦，已灭之邦，冀理外之奇举，不亦闇哉！

translations.literal: Deng Ai's entry Jiangyou—soldiers few—Wei advance could not rouse integrity under Mianzhu—retreat could not marshal five generals—protect Shu lord—thinking later scheme—yet reversed between rebel and loyal—hoping against hope in hard meeting—using weak country—yet repeatedly viewing troops in three Qin—already extinguished state—hoping manage outer extraordinary rising—is this not dim!
translations.idiomatic: He faults Jiang Wei for neither saving Mianzhu nor the emperor yet gambling on wild stratagems.

sentences.zh: ○臣松之以为盛之讥维，又为不当。

translations.literal: ○ Your servant Pei Songzhi thought Sheng's ridicule Wei—again was improper.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Songzhi rejects Sun Sheng’s harsh verdict.

sentences.zh: 于时锺会大众既造剑阁，维与诸将列营守险，会不得进，已议还计，全蜀之功，几乎立矣。

translations.literal: At that time Zhong Hui great host already reached Jiange—Wei with various generals arrayed camps guarding defile—Hui could not advance—already debated return plan—whole Shu merit—almost established.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Wei held Jiange until Zhong Hui nearly withdrew—Shu almost survived.

sentences.zh: 但邓艾诡道傍入，出於其后，诸葛瞻既败，成都自溃。

translations.literal: But Deng Ai crooked path side entered—came out behind them—Zhuge Zhan already defeated—Chengdu self-collapsed.
translations.idiomatic: Deng Ai slipped past him; Zhuge Zhan fell and Chengdu collapsed.

sentences.zh: 维若回军救内，则会乘其背。

translations.literal: If Wei turned army to save inside—then Hui would ride his back.
translations.idiomatic: Had Jiang Wei raced home Zhong Hui would have struck his rear.

sentences.zh: 当时之势，焉得两济？

translations.literal: At that time situation—how obtain both rescue?
translations.idiomatic: No force could cover both fronts.

sentences.zh: 而责维不能奋节绵竹，拥卫蜀主，非其理也。

translations.literal: Yet blame Wei cannot rouse integrity Mianzhu—protect Shu lord—not its principle.
translations.idiomatic: Blaming him for missing Mianzhu is unfair.

sentences.zh: 会欲尽坑魏将以举大事，授维重兵，使为前驱。

translations.literal: Hui wished fully bury Wei generals to raise great affair—gave Wei heavy troops—made front vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong Hui meant to slaughter Wei generals and gave Jiang Wei a leading role.

sentences.zh: 若令魏将皆死，兵事在维手，杀会复蜀，不为难矣。

translations.literal: If order Wei generals all dead—military affairs in Wei's hand—kill Hui restore Shu—not hard.
translations.idiomatic: Had the plot killed Zhong Hui, Shu might rise again.

sentences.zh: 夫功成理外，然后为奇，不可以事有差牙，而抑谓不然。

translations.literal: Husband merit complete manage outer—then becomes extraordinary—cannot because affair has mismatch—and suppress say not so.
translations.idiomatic: Genius lies in seizing the unlikely moment—small slips do not negate the gambit.

sentences.zh: 设使田单之计，邂逅不会，复可谓之愚闇哉！〉

translations.literal: Suppose Tian Dan's plan—chance not meeting—again can call it foolish dim!>
translations.idiomatic: Would Tian Dan be ‘foolish’ if his fire-ox ruse had failed?

sentences.zh: 欲授維兵五萬人，使為前驅。

translations.literal: Wished grant Wei troops fifty thousand—make front vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong Hui planned to give Jiang Wei fifty thousand men as van.

sentences.zh: 魏將士憤發，殺會及維，維妻子皆伏誅。

translations.literal: Wei officers rose in anger—killed Hui and Wei—Wei's wife and children all executed.
translations.idiomatic: Wei troops mutinied and killed both men; Jiang Wei’s family perished with them.

sentences.zh: 〈世语曰：维死时见剖，胆如

translations.literal: < Shiyu says: When Wei died—saw dissection—gall bladder like
translations.idiomatic: < The Shiyu adds that when opened his gall was as large as

translations.literal: (dou measure)
translations.idiomatic: a peck measure

translations.literal: large.>
translations.idiomatic: —enormous.>

sentences.zh: 郤正著論論維曰：「姜伯約據上將之重，處群臣之右。

translations.literal: Xi Zheng wrote a treatise discussing Wei, saying, "Jiang Boyue held highest general's weight—stood to the right of the host of ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Xi Zheng’s essay: Jiang Wei held a marshal’s power and outranked the court.

sentences.zh: 宅舍弊薄，資財無餘，側室無妾媵之褻，後庭無聲樂之娛。

translations.literal: House and dwelling dilapidated thin—assets and wealth without surplus—side chambers without concubine attendants' intimacy—rear court without music's entertainment.
translations.idiomatic: He lived in a mean house, kept no concubines, and spent nothing on music.

sentences.zh: 衣服取供，輿馬取備，飲食節制，不奢不約，官給費用，隨手消盡；

translations.literal: Clothes take what supplies—carriages and horses take what suffices—drink and food measured and restrained—not extravagant not constrained—official stipend expenses—follow hand and vanish.
translations.idiomatic: He dressed and traveled modestly, spent his salary as it came, and saved nothing.

sentences.zh: 察其所以然者，非以激貪厲濁，抑情自割也。

translations.literal: Observing his reason for being so—not to excite against greed and encourage filth—suppress feeling and self-cut.
translations.idiomatic: This was not posturing for reputation—he simply needed no more.

sentences.zh: 直謂如是為足，不在多求。

translations.literal: Straight said like this is enough—does not seek more.
translations.idiomatic: He was content with little.

sentences.zh: 凡人之談，常譽成毀敗，扶高抑下，鹹以姜維投厝無所，身死宗滅，以是貶削，不復料擿，異乎《春秋》褒貶之義矣。

translations.literal: Ordinary men's talk—often praise success and destroy failure—prop high and press low—all because Jiang Wei had no place to cast—body died and clan extinguished—thereby belittle and cut—no longer examine—different from Chunqiu praise and blame meaning.
translations.idiomatic: People mock his fall, yet the Spring and Autumn Annals judge deeds, not outcomes alone.

sentences.zh: 如姜維之樂學不倦，清素節約，自一時之儀表也。」

translations.literal: As for Jiang Wei's delight in study without weariness—pure and frugal and economical—he was a model of the age."
translations.idiomatic: For love of learning and clean living he was a paragon of his time."

sentences.zh: 〈孙盛曰：异哉郤氏之论也！

translations.literal: < Sun Sheng said: Strange is Xi clan's treatise!
translations.idiomatic: Sun Sheng retorts: Xi Zheng is wrong.

sentences.zh: 夫士虽百行，操业万殊，至於忠孝义节，百行之冠冕也。

translations.literal: Though a gentleman has hundred conducts—occupations ten thousand different—reaching loyalty, filiality, duty, and integrity—these are the hundred conducts' cap.
translations.idiomatic: Loyalty, filial piety, duty, and honor crown all other virtues.

sentences.zh: 姜维策名魏室，而外奔蜀朝，违君徇利，不可谓忠；

translations.literal: Jiang Wei pledged name to Wei house—yet outside fled to Shu court—disobeying lord to pursue profit—cannot call loyal.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Wei served Wei, then ran to Shu—disloyal to his first master.

sentences.zh: 捐亲苟免，不可谓孝；

translations.literal: Abandoning kin to seek escape—cannot call filial.
translations.idiomatic: He left his mother—unfilial.

sentences.zh: 害加旧邦，不可谓义；

translations.literal: Harm added to old state—cannot call righteous.
translations.idiomatic: He warred on his native north—unrighteous.

sentences.zh: 败不死难，不可谓节；

translations.literal: Defeated yet not dying in hardship—cannot call intrepid.
translations.idiomatic: He did not die with his defeated state—lacking constancy.

sentences.zh: 且德政未敷而疲民以逞，居御侮之任而致敌丧守，於夫智勇，莫可云也：凡斯六者，维无一焉。

translations.literal: Moreover virtue and government not spread yet wearied the people to show off—dwelt in office to repel insult yet brought enemy to lose the guard—concerning wisdom and courage—none can say: all these six—Wei has not one.
translations.idiomatic: He exhausted Shu without governing well and lost every pass—wisdom and courage fail him on all six counts.

sentences.zh: 实有魏之逋臣，亡国之乱相，而云人之仪表，斯亦惑矣。

translations.literal: Truly Wei's fugitive subject—extinct state's disorder minister—yet say people's model—this also is deluded.
translations.idiomatic: He was a renegade and a traitor, not a paragon.

sentences.zh: 纵维好书而微自藻洁，岂异夫盗者分财之义，而程、郑降阶之善也？

translations.literal: Even if Wei loved books and slightly kept self clean—how different robbers dividing spoils' meaning—and Cheng, Zheng descending step's good!
translations.idiomatic: Thrifty study cannot redeem those crimes—like praising a thief for sharing loot.

sentences.zh: 臣松之以为郤正此论，取其可称，不谓维始终行事皆可准则也。

translations.literal: Your servant Pei Songzhi thought Xi Zheng this treatise—takes what can be praised—does not say Wei's from beginning to end conduct all can be standard.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Songzhi: Xi Zheng meant only to praise study and thrift, not to bless every act.

sentences.zh: 所云“一时仪表”，止在好学与俭素耳。

translations.literal: What is called 'model of the time'—stops at love of study and frugality.
translations.idiomatic: The 'paragon' line referred only to scholarship and simplicity.

sentences.zh: 本传及魏略皆云维本无叛心，以急逼归蜀。

translations.literal: Main tradition and Wei Lue both say Wei originally had no rebel heart—compelled to return to Shu.
translations.idiomatic: The standard histories say he had no treason in mind when he joined Shu—only force.

sentences.zh: 盛相讥贬，惟可责其背母。

translations.literal: Sheng's mutual ridicule and belittle—only can blame his abandoning mother.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Sheng may rebuke him mainly for leaving his mother.

sentences.zh: 餘既过苦，又非所以难郤正也。〉

translations.literal: The rest already too harsh—also not the reason to refute Xi Zheng.>
translations.idiomatic: The rest of Sheng’s attack overreaches.>

sentences.zh: 維昔所俱至蜀，梁緒官至大鴻臚，尹賞執金吾，梁虔大長秋，皆先蜀亡沒。

translations.literal: Those who with Wei together came to Shu—Liang Xu reached grand astrologer—Yin Shang held gold qu—Liang Qian great privy treasurer—all before Shu perished passed.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Wei’s Tianshui colleagues—Liang Xu, Yin Shang, Liang Qian—rose high and died before the fall.

sentences.zh: 评曰：蒋琬方整有威重，费祎宽济而博爱，咸承诸葛之成规，因循而不革，是以边境无虞，邦家和一，然犹未尽治小之宜，居静之理也。

translations.literal: The evaluation says: Jiang Wan was square, orderly, and awesome; Fei Yi was broad, helpful, and universal in love; both inherited Zhuge's completed regulations—followed and did not reform—therefore border had no worry—state and family harmonized as one—yet still not fully achieve governing small's fitness—dwelling still's principle.
translations.idiomatic: The verdict: Jiang Wan and Fei Yi continued Zhuge Liang’s policy—calm borders and stable court—though critics say they never mastered ‘ruling a small state with a light touch.’

sentences.zh: 〈臣松之以为蒋、费为相，克遵画一，未尝徇功妄动，有所亏丧，外卻骆谷之师，内保宁缉之实，治小之宜，居静之理，何以过於此哉！

translations.literal: < Your servant Pei Songzhi thought Jiang, Fei as chancellors—able to follow single plan—never bent to merit and rashly moved—had loss and harm—outer repelled Lu Valley's army—inner preserved peace and order's reality—governing small's fitness—dwelling still's principle—how surpass this!
translations.idiomatic: Pei Songzhi: they repelled Cao Shuang and kept the peace—what better small-state policy?

sentences.zh: 今讥其未尽而不著其事，故使览者不知所谓也。〉

translations.literal: Now ridicule their not exhaust yet not show the matters—therefore make readers not know the so-called.>
translations.idiomatic: The text faults them without evidence.>

sentences.zh: 姜维粗有文武，志立功名，而玩众黩旅，明断不周，终致陨毙。

translations.literal: Jiang Wei roughly had civil and military—aimed to establish merit and fame—yet played with the host and disgraced the host—clear judgment not thorough—ultimately met fall and death.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Wei had talent and ambition but wasted his army and died for it.

sentences.zh: 老子有云：“治大国者犹烹小鲜。

translations.literal: Laozi said, "Governing a great state is like cooking a small fish.
translations.idiomatic: Laozi said that ruling a great kingdom is like frying a small fish—handle it gently.

sentences.zh: ”况於区区蕞尔，而可屡扰乎哉？

translations.literal: " How much more a tiny trifling mite—yet can repeatedly disturb!
translations.idiomatic: " How much more must this hold for a pocket-sized realm that cannot endure endless meddling?

sentences.zh: 〈干宝曰：姜维为蜀相，国亡主辱弗之死，而死於锺会之乱，惜哉！

translations.literal: < Gan Bao said: Jiang Wei as Shu chancellor—state perished lord shamed—did not die for that—yet died in Zhong Hui's disorder—pity!
translations.idiomatic: < Gan Bao laments: Jiang Wei survived his sovereign’s shame yet died in Zhong Hui’s riot instead of with his king.

sentences.zh: 非死之难，处死之难也。

translations.literal: Not death is hard—disposing death is hard.
translations.idiomatic: The hardship lies not in dying but in choosing the proper death.

sentences.zh: 是以古之烈士，见危授命，投节如归，非不爱死也，固知命之不长而惧不得其所也。〉

translations.literal: Therefore ancient ardent knights—seeing peril granted life—cast aside integrity like returning home—not that they did not love death—indeed knew life not long and feared not obtaining their place.>
translations.idiomatic: Heroes of old faced doom with eyes open and threw away rank like old clothes—not because they despised life, but because they feared living without purpose.>
